   104→    queue_section: dict[str, Any] = {

   108→    payload: dict[str, Any] = {

   122→            member_ids = set(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   123→            clusters_summary.append({
   124→                "name": name,
   125→                "description": cluster.get("description"),
   126→                "item_count": len(member_ids),
   127→            })
   128→        payload["plan"] = {

   131→            "clusters": clusters_summary,

   134→            "plan_overrides_narrative": True,

   140→def render_markdown(items: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> str:
   141→    """Render queue items as markdown."""
   142→    lines = [
   143→        "# Desloppify Next Queue",
   144→        "",
   145→        "| Kind | Confidence | Summary | Command |",
   146→        "|------|------------|---------|---------|",
   147→    ]
   148→    for item in items:
   149→        kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   150→        conf = item.get("confidence", "medium")
   151→        summary = item.get("summary", "").replace("|", "\\|")
   152→        command = (item.get("primary_command", "") or "").replace("|", "\\|")
   153→        lines.append(f"| {kind} | {conf} | {summary} | {command} |")
   154→    lines.append("")
   155→    return "\n".join(lines)

   158→def write_output_file(

   162→    *,
   163→    safe_write_text_fn,
   164→    colorize_fn,
   165→) -> bool:
   166→    """Persist payload to file and print success/failure hints."""
   167→    try:

   169→        print(colorize_fn(f"Wrote {item_count} items to {output_file}", "green"))
   170→    except OSError as exc:
   171→        payload["output_error"] = str(exc)

   210→                active = []

   213→            if not active and not queued:

   221→                segments.append(f"#{idx + 1}:{secs}s")
   222→            if len(active) > 6:
   223→                segments.append(f"+{len(active) - 6} more")
   224→            queued_segment = ""
   225→            if queued:
   226→                queued_segment = f", queued {len(queued)}"
   227→            print(
   228→                colorize_fn(

   106→    GodRule(
   107→        "custom_hooks", "custom hooks", lambda c: c.metrics.get("custom_hooks", 0), 8
   108→    ),
   109→    GodRule("hook_total", "total hooks", lambda c: c.metrics.get("hook_total", 0), 10),
   110→]
   111→
   112→TS_SKIP_NAMES = {
   113→    "index.ts",
   114→    "index.tsx",
   115→    "types.ts",
   116→    "types.tsx",
   117→    "constants.ts",
   118→    "constants.tsx",
   119→    "utils.ts",
   120→    "utils.tsx",
   121→    "helpers.ts",
   122→    "helpers.tsx",
   123→    "settings.ts",
   124→    "settings.tsx",
   125→    "main.ts",
   126→    "main.tsx",
   127→    "App.tsx",
   128→    "vite-env.d.ts",
   129→}
   130→
   131→TS_SKIP_DIRS = {"src/shared/components/ui"}
   132→
   133→
   134→# ── Phase runners ──────────────────────────────────────────
   135→
   136→
   137→def phase_logs(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   138→    log_result = logs_detector_mod.detect_logs_result(path)
   139→    log_entries = log_result.entries
   140→    total_files = log_result.population_size
   141→    log_groups: dict[tuple, list] = defaultdict(list)
   142→    for e in log_entries:
   143→        log_groups[(e["file"], e["tag"])].append(e)
   144→    results = []
   145→    for (file, tag), entries in log_groups.items():
   146→        results.append(
   147→            make_issue(
   148→                "logs",
   149→                file,
   150→                tag,
   151→                tier=1,
   152→                confidence="high",
   153→                summary=f"{len(entries)} tagged logs [{tag}]",
   154→                detail={
   155→                    "count": len(entries),
   156→                    "lines": [e["line"] for e in entries[:20]],
   157→                },
   158→            )
   159→        )
   160→    log(f"         {len(log_entries)} instances → {len(results)} issues")
   161→    return results, {"logs": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_files)}
   162→
   163→
   164→def phase_unused(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   165→    entries, total_files = unused_detector_mod.detect_unused(path)
   166→    return make_unused_issues(entries, log), {
   167→        "unused": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_files),
   168→    }

   170→
   171→def phase_exports(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   172→    export_entries, total_exports = exports_detector_mod.detect_dead_exports(path)
   173→    results = []
   174→    for e in export_entries:
   175→        results.append(
   176→            make_issue(
   177→                "exports",
   178→                e["file"],
   179→                e["name"],
   180→                tier=2,
   181→                confidence="high",
   182→                summary=f"Dead export: {e['name']}",
   183→                detail={"line": e.get("line"), "kind": e.get("kind")},
   184→            )
   185→        )
   186→    log(f"         {len(export_entries)} instances → {len(results)} issues")
   187→    return results, {"exports": total_exports}
   188→
   189→
   190→def phase_deprecated(
   191→    path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract
   192→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   193→    dep_result = deprecated_detector_mod.detect_deprecated_result(path)
   194→    dep_entries = dep_result.entries
   195→    total_deprecated = dep_result.population_size
   196→    results = []
   197→    for e in dep_entries:
   198→        if e["kind"] == "property":
   199→            continue
   200→        tier = 1 if e["importers"] == 0 else 3
   201→        results.append(
   202→            make_issue(
   203→                "deprecated",
   204→                e["file"],
   205→                e["symbol"],
   206→                tier=tier,
   207→                confidence="high",
   208→                summary=f"Deprecated: {e['symbol']} ({e['importers']} importers)"
   209→                + (" → safe to delete" if e["importers"] == 0 else ""),
   210→                detail={"importers": e["importers"], "line": e["line"]},
   211→            )
   212→        )
   213→    log(
   214→        f"         {len(dep_entries)} instances → {len(results)} issues (properties suppressed)"
   215→    )
   216→    return results, {"deprecated": total_deprecated}
   217→
   218→
   219→def phase_structural(
   220→    path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract
   221→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   222→    structural: dict[str, dict] = {}
   223→
   224→    large_entries, file_count = large_detector_mod.detect_large_files(
   225→        path,
   226→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   227→        threshold=lang.large_threshold,
   228→    )
   229→    for e in large_entries:
   230→        add_structural_signal(
   231→            structural, e["file"], f"large ({e['loc']} LOC)", {"loc": e["loc"]}
   232→        )
   233→
   234→    complexity_entries, _ = complexity_detector_mod.detect_complexity(
   235→        path,
   236→        signals=TS_COMPLEXITY_SIGNALS,
   237→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   238→        threshold=lang.complexity_threshold,
   239→    )
   240→    for e in complexity_entries:
   241→        add_structural_signal(
   242→            structural,
   243→            e["file"],
   244→            f"complexity score {e['score']}",
   245→            {"complexity_score": e["score"], "complexity_signals": e["signals"]},
   246→        )
   247→        lang.complexity_map[e["file"]] = e["score"]
   248→
   249→    god_entries, _ = gods_detector_mod.detect_gods(
   250→        extract_ts_components(path), TS_GOD_RULES, min_reasons=2
   251→    )
   252→    for e in god_entries:
   253→        add_structural_signal(
   254→            structural,
   255→            e["file"],
   256→            f"{e['detail'].get('hook_total', 0)} hooks ({', '.join(e['reasons'][:2])})",
   257→            {
   258→                "hook_total": e["detail"].get("hook_total", 0),
   259→                "hook_reasons": e["reasons"],
   260→            },
   261→        )
   262→
   263→    concern_entries, _ = concerns_detector_mod.detect_mixed_concerns(path)
   264→    for e in concern_entries:
   265→        add_structural_signal(
   266→            structural,
   267→            e["file"],
   268→            f"mixed: {', '.join(e['concerns'][:3])}",
   269→            {"concerns": e["concerns"]},
   270→        )
   271→
   272→    results = merge_structural_signals(structural, log)
   273→
   274→    # Flat directories (too many files → missing sub-organization)
   275→    flat_entries, dir_count = flat_dirs_detector_mod.detect_flat_dirs(
   276→        path,
   277→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   278→        config=flat_dirs_detector_mod.FlatDirDetectionConfig(),
   279→    )
   280→    for e in flat_entries:
   281→        child_dir_count = int(e.get("child_dir_count", 0))
   282→        combined_score = int(e.get("combined_score", e.get("file_count", 0)))
   283→        results.append(
   284→            make_issue(
   285→                "flat_dirs",
   286→                e["directory"],
   287→                "",
   288→                tier=3,
   289→                confidence="medium",
   290→                summary=flat_dirs_detector_mod.format_flat_dir_summary(e),
   291→                detail={
   292→                    "file_count": e["file_count"],
   293→                    "child_dir_count": child_dir_count,
   294→                    "combined_score": combined_score,
   295→                    "kind": e.get("kind", "overload"),
   296→                    "parent_sibling_count": int(e.get("parent_sibling_count", 0)),
   297→                    "wrapper_item_count": int(e.get("wrapper_item_count", 0)),
   298→                    "sparse_child_count": int(e.get("sparse_child_count", 0)),
   299→                    "sparse_child_ratio": float(e.get("sparse_child_ratio", 0.0)),
   300→                    "sparse_child_file_threshold": int(
   301→                        e.get("sparse_child_file_threshold", 0)
   302→                    ),
   303→                },
   304→            )
   305→        )
   306→    if flat_entries:
   307→        log(
   308→            f"         flat dirs: {len(flat_entries)} overloaded directories "
   309→            "(files/subdirs/combined)"
   310→        )
   311→
   312→    # TS-specific: props bloat
   313→    props_thresh = lang.props_threshold
   314→    prop_entries, prop_count = props_detector_mod.detect_prop_interface_bloat(
   315→        path, threshold=props_thresh
   316→    )
   317→    for e in prop_entries:
   318→        pc = e["prop_count"]
   319→        # Tiered severity: 15-29=low, 30-49=medium, 50+=high
   320→        if pc >= 50:
   321→            conf, tier = "high", 4
   322→        elif pc >= 30:
   323→            conf, tier = "medium", 3
   324→        else:
   325→            conf, tier = "low", 3
   326→        results.append(
   327→            make_issue(
   328→                "props",
   329→                e["file"],
   330→                e["interface"],
   331→                tier=tier,
   332→                confidence=conf,
   333→                summary=f"Bloated {e.get('kind', 'props')}: {e['interface']} ({pc} fields)",
   334→                detail={
   335→                    "prop_count": pc,
   336→                    "line": e["line"],
   337→                    "kind": e.get("kind", "props"),
   338→                },
   339→            )
   340→        )
   341→
   342→    # TS-specific: passthrough components
   343→    pt_entries = detect_passthrough_components(path)
   344→    for e in pt_entries:
   345→        results.append(
   346→            make_issue(
   347→                "props",
   348→                e["file"],
   349→                f"passthrough::{e['component']}",
   350→                tier=e["tier"],
   351→                confidence=e["confidence"],
   352→                summary=f"Passthrough component: {e['component']} "
   353→                f"({e['passthrough']}/{e['total_props']} props forwarded, {e['ratio']:.0%})",
   354→                detail={
   355→                    "passthrough": e["passthrough"],
   356→                    "total_props": e["total_props"],
   357→                    "ratio": e["ratio"],
   358→                    "line": e["line"],
   359→                    "passthrough_props": e["passthrough_props"],
   360→                    "direct_props": e["direct_props"],
   361→                },
   362→            )
   363→        )
   364→    potentials = {
   365→        "structural": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, file_count),
   366→        "flat_dirs": dir_count,
   367→        "props": max(prop_count, len(pt_entries)) if prop_count else len(pt_entries),
   368→    }
   369→    return results, potentials
   370→
   371→
   372→def _make_boundary_issues(
   373→    single_entries: list[dict],
   374→    path: Path,
   375→    graph: dict,
   376→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   377→    shared_prefix: str,
   378→    tools_prefix: str,
   379→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   380→    """Create boundary-candidate issues, deduplicated against single-use."""
   381→    single_use_emitted = set()
   382→    for e in single_entries:
   383→        is_size_ok = 50 <= e["loc"] <= 200
   384→        is_colocated = lang.get_area and (
   385→            lang.get_area(rel(e["file"])) == lang.get_area(e["sole_importer"])
   386→        )
   387→        if not is_size_ok and not is_colocated:
   388→            single_use_emitted.add(rel(e["file"]))
   389→
   390→    results = []
   391→    deduped = 0
   392→    boundary_entries, total_shared = coupling_detector_mod.detect_boundary_candidates(
   393→        path,
   394→        graph,
   395→        shared_prefix=shared_prefix,
   396→        tools_prefix=tools_prefix,
   397→        skip_basenames={"index.ts", "index.tsx"},
   398→    )
   399→    for e in boundary_entries:
   400→        if rel(e["file"]) in single_use_emitted:
   401→            deduped += 1
   402→            continue
   403→        results.append(
   404→            make_issue(
   405→                "coupling",
   406→                e["file"],
   407→                f"boundary::{e['sole_tool']}",
   408→                tier=3,
   409→                confidence="medium",
   410→                summary=f"Boundary candidate ({e['loc']} LOC): only used by {e['sole_tool']} "
   411→                f"({e['importer_count']} importers)",
   412→                detail={
   413→                    "sole_tool": e["sole_tool"],
   414→                    "importer_count": e["importer_count"],
   415→                    "loc": e["loc"],
   416→                },
   417→            )
   418→        )
   419→    if deduped:
   420→        log(f"         ({deduped} boundary candidates skipped — covered by single_use)")
   421→    return results, total_shared
   422→
   423→
   424→def phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   425→    results = []
   426→    graph = deps_detector_mod.build_dep_graph(path)
   427→    lang.dep_graph = graph
   428→    zm = lang.zone_map
   429→
   430→    # Single-use (shared helper)
   431→    single_entries, single_candidates = (
   432→        single_use_detector_mod.detect_single_use_abstractions(
   433→            path, graph, barrel_names=lang.barrel_names
   434→        )
   435→    )
   436→    single_entries = filter_entries(zm, single_entries, "single_use")
   437→    results.extend(
   438→        make_single_use_issues(
   439→            single_entries, lang.get_area, skip_dir_names={"commands"}, stderr_fn=log
   440→        )
   441→    )
   442→    src_path = get_src_path()
   443→    shared_prefix = f"{src_path}/shared/"
   444→    tools_prefix = f"{src_path}/tools/"
   445→    coupling_entries, coupling_edge_counts = coupling_detector_mod.detect_coupling_violations(
   446→        path, graph, shared_prefix=shared_prefix, tools_prefix=tools_prefix
   447→    )
   448→    coupling_entries = filter_entries(zm, coupling_entries, "coupling")
   449→    for e in coupling_entries:
   450→        results.append(
   451→            make_issue(
   452→                "coupling",
   453→                e["file"],
   454→                e["target"],
   455→                tier=2,
   456→                confidence="high",
   457→                summary=f"Backwards coupling: shared imports {e['target']} (tool: {e['tool']})",
   458→                detail={
   459→                    "target": e["target"],
   460→                    "tool": e["tool"],
   461→                    "direction": e["direction"],
   462→                },
   463→            )
   464→        )
   465→
   466→    # TS-specific: boundary candidates (deduplicated against single-use)
   467→    boundary_issues, _ = _make_boundary_issues(
   468→        single_entries, path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
   469→    )
   470→    results.extend(boundary_issues)
   471→
   472→    # TS-specific: cross-tool imports
   473→    cross_tool, cross_edge_counts = coupling_detector_mod.detect_cross_tool_imports(
   474→        path, graph, tools_prefix=tools_prefix
   475→    )
   476→    cross_tool = filter_entries(zm, cross_tool, "coupling")
   477→    for e in cross_tool:
   478→        results.append(
   479→            make_issue(
   480→                "coupling",
   481→                e["file"],
   482→                e["target"],
   483→                tier=2,
   484→                confidence="high",
   485→                summary=f"Cross-tool import: {e['source_tool']}→{e['target_tool']} ({e['target']})",
   486→                detail={
   487→                    "target": e["target"],
   488→                    "source_tool": e["source_tool"],
   489→                    "target_tool": e["target_tool"],
   490→                    "direction": e["direction"],
   491→                },
   492→            )
   493→        )
   494→    if cross_tool:
   495→        log(f"         cross-tool: {len(cross_tool)} imports")
   496→
   497→    # Cycles + orphaned (shared helpers)
   498→    cycle_entries, _ = graph_detector_mod.detect_cycles(graph)
   499→    cycle_entries = filter_entries(zm, cycle_entries, "cycles", file_key="files")
   500→    results.extend(make_cycle_issues(cycle_entries, log))
   501→    orphan_entries, total_graph_files = orphaned_detector_mod.detect_orphaned_files(
   502→        path,
   503→        graph,
   504→        extensions=lang.extensions,
   505→        options=orphaned_detector_mod.OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   506→            extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   507→            extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   508→            dynamic_import_finder=deps_detector_mod.build_dynamic_import_targets,
   509→            alias_resolver=deps_detector_mod.ts_alias_resolver,
   510→        ),
   511→    )
   512→    orphan_entries = filter_entries(zm, orphan_entries, "orphaned")
   513→    results.extend(make_orphaned_issues(orphan_entries, log))
   514→
   515→    # Re-export facades (shared detector)
   516→    facade_entries, _ = facade_detector_mod.detect_reexport_facades(graph)
   517→    facade_entries = filter_entries(zm, facade_entries, "facade")
   518→    results.extend(make_facade_issues(facade_entries, log))
   519→
   520→    # TS-specific: pattern consistency
   521→    pattern_result = patterns_detector_mod.detect_pattern_anomalies_result(path)
   522→    pattern_entries = pattern_result.entries
   523→    total_areas = pattern_result.population_size
   524→    for e in pattern_entries:
   525→        results.append(
   526→            make_issue(
   527→                "patterns",
   528→                e["area"],
   529→                e["family"],
   530→                tier=3,
   531→                confidence=e.get("confidence", "low"),
   532→                summary=f"Competing patterns ({e['family']}): {e['review'][:120]}",
   533→                detail={
   534→                    "family": e["family"],
   535→                    "patterns_used": e["patterns_used"],
   536→                    "pattern_count": e["pattern_count"],
   537→                    "review": e["review"],
   538→                },
   539→            )
   540→        )
   541→
   542→    # TS-specific: naming consistency
   543→    naming_entries, total_dirs = naming_detector_mod.detect_naming_inconsistencies(
   544→        path,
   545→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   546→        skip_names=TS_SKIP_NAMES,
   547→        skip_dirs=TS_SKIP_DIRS,
   548→    )
   549→    for e in naming_entries:
   550→        results.append(
   551→            make_issue(
   552→                "naming",
   553→                e["directory"],
   554→                e["minority"],
   555→                tier=3,
   556→                confidence="low",
   557→                summary=f"Naming inconsistency: {e['minority_count']} {e['minority']} files "
   558→                f"in {e['majority']}-majority dir ({e['total_files']} total)",
   559→                detail={
   560→                    "majority": e["majority"],
   561→                    "majority_count": e["majority_count"],
   562→                    "minority": e["minority"],
   563→                    "minority_count": e["minority_count"],
   564→                    "outliers": e["outliers"],
   565→                },
   566→            )
   567→        )
   568→    log(f"         → {len(results)} coupling/structural issues total")
   569→    coupling_edges = coupling_edge_counts.eligible_edges
   570→    cross_edges = cross_edge_counts.eligible_edges
   571→    potentials = {
   572→        "single_use": adjust_potential(zm, single_candidates),
   573→        "coupling": coupling_edges + cross_edges,
   574→        "cycles": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   575→        "orphaned": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   576→        "patterns": total_areas,
   577→        "naming": total_dirs,
   578→        "facade": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   579→    }
   580→    return results, potentials
   581→
   582→
   583→def phase_smells(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   584→    smell_entries, total_smell_files = smells_detector_mod.detect_smells(path)
   585→    results = make_smell_issues(smell_entries, log)
   586→
   587→    # TS-specific: React state sync anti-patterns
   588→    react_entries, total_effects = react_detector_mod.detect_state_sync(path)
   589→    for e in react_entries:
   590→        setter_str = ", ".join(e["setters"])
   591→        results.append(
   592→            make_issue(
   593→                "react",
   594→                e["file"],
   595→                setter_str,
   596→                tier=3,
   597→                confidence="medium",
   598→                summary=f"State sync anti-pattern: useEffect only calls {setter_str}",
   599→                detail={"line": e["line"], "setters": e["setters"]},
   600→            )
   601→        )
   602→    if react_entries:
   603→        log(f"         react: {len(react_entries)} state sync anti-patterns")
   604→
   605→    # TS-specific: Context provider nesting depth
   606→    nesting_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_context_nesting(path)
   607→    for e in nesting_entries:
   608→        providers_str = " → ".join(e["providers"][:5])
   609→        results.append(
   610→            make_issue(
   611→                "react",
   612→                e["file"],
   613→                f"nesting::{e['depth']}",
   614→                tier=3,
   615→                confidence="medium",
   616→                summary=f"Deep provider nesting ({e['depth']} levels): {providers_str}",
   617→                detail={"depth": e["depth"], "providers": e["providers"]},
   618→            )
   619→        )
   620→    if nesting_entries:
   621→        log(f"         react: {len(nesting_entries)} deep provider nesting")
   622→
   623→    # TS-specific: Hook return bloat
   624→    hook_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_hook_return_bloat(path)
   625→    for e in hook_entries:
   626→        results.append(
   627→            make_issue(
   628→                "react",
   629→                e["file"],
   630→                f"hook_bloat::{e['hook']}",
   631→                tier=3,
   632→                confidence="medium",
   633→                summary=f"Hook return bloat: {e['hook']} returns {e['field_count']} fields",
   634→                detail={
   635→                    "hook": e["hook"],
   636→                    "field_count": e["field_count"],
   637→                    "line": e["line"],
   638→                },
   639→            )
   640→        )
   641→    if hook_entries:
   642→        log(f"         react: {len(hook_entries)} bloated hook returns")
   643→
   644→    # TS-specific: Boolean state explosion
   645→    bool_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_boolean_state_explosion(path)
   646→    for e in bool_entries:
   647→        states_str = ", ".join(e["states"][:5])
   648→        results.append(
   649→            make_issue(
   650→                "react",
   651→                e["file"],
   652→                f"bool_state::{e['prefix']}",
   653→                tier=3,
   654→                confidence="low",
   655→                summary=f"Boolean state explosion: {e['count']} boolean useState hooks ({states_str})",
   656→                detail={
   657→                    "count": e["count"],
   658→                    "setters": e["setters"],
   659→                    "states": e["states"],
   660→                    "line": e["line"],
   661→                },
   662→            )
   663→        )
   664→    if bool_entries:
   665→        log(f"         react: {len(bool_entries)} boolean state explosions")
   666→
   667→    return results, {
   668→        "smells": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_smell_files),

The `reconcile_plan_post_scan` function previously wrapped the entire body (load, all sync/reconciliation logic, and save) in a single `try/except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS`. This meant any `OSError`, `ImportError`, `AttributeError`, etc. raised by the internal reconciliation logic would be silently caught and logged as "skipped."

Refactored to two narrow try/except blocks:
- **Around `load_plan()`:** catches `PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS` and returns early with a warning if loading fails.
- **Around `save_plan()`:** catches `PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS` and logs a warning if saving fails after successful reconciliation.

Internal sync/reconciliation errors (bugs, unexpected state, etc.) now propagate naturally instead of being swallowed.

def _serialize_cluster_member(member: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:

        "confidence": member.get("confidence"),
        "detector": member.get("detector"),
        ...
    }

## 1. `execution.py` -- `do_run_batches()` decomposition

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/batch/execution.py`

Extracted 4 helper functions from the ~505-line `do_run_batches()`:

- **`_build_progress_reporter(...)`** -- Factory that builds the `_report_progress` closure. Takes all the shared state (batch_positions, batch_status, stall_warned_batches, etc.) as parameters and returns the callback function. This was a ~120-line nested function.

- **`_handle_heartbeat(...)`** -- Extracted from within the progress reporter to handle heartbeat events specifically (active/queued batch display, stall warnings). This was the largest branch of `_report_progress`.

- **`_collect_and_reconcile_results(...)`** -- Collects batch results via the injected `collect_batch_results_fn`, then reconciles per-batch status entries (succeeded/failed/missing_output/parse_failed). Returns `(batch_results, successful_indexes, failures, failure_set)`.

- **`_merge_and_write_results(...)`** -- Merges batch results, enriches with review scope/provenance/coverage metadata, writes the merged JSON to disk, and prints quality info. Returns the `merged_path`.

- **`_import_and_finalize(...)`** -- Imports merged results into state via `do_import_fn` and optionally runs a followup scan. Handles SystemExit/Exception logging.

The main `do_run_batches()` orchestrator still owns setup, policy resolution, artifact preparation, dry-run handling, execution, and the KeyboardInterrupt handler. It calls the helpers for progress reporting, result collection, merging, and import.

    11→    completed = getattr(si, "completed_clusters", [])
    12→    resolved = getattr(si, "resolved_issues", {})
    13→    open_issues = getattr(si, "open_issues", {})
    14→
    15→    _print_completed_clusters(completed)
    16→    _print_resolved_issues(resolved)
    17→    recurring = _print_recurring_patterns(open_issues, resolved)
    18→    if not recurring and not completed and not resolved:
    19→        print(colorize("\n  First triage — no prior work to compare against.", "dim"))
    20→        print(colorize("  Focus your reflect report on your strategy:", "yellow"))
    21→        print(

    23→                "  - How will you resolve contradictions you identified in observe?",

    26→        )
    27→        print(colorize("  - Which issues will you cluster together vs defer?", "dim"))
    28→        print(colorize("  - What's the overall arc of work and why?", "dim"))
    29→
    30→
    31→def _print_completed_clusters(completed: list[dict]) -> None:
    32→    """Print completed cluster context for reflect stage."""
    33→    if not completed:
    34→        return
    35→    print(colorize("\n  Previously completed clusters:", "cyan"))
    36→    for cluster in completed[:10]:
    37→        name = cluster.get("name", "?")

    43→        for step in cluster.get("action_steps", [])[:3]:
    44→            print(colorize(f"      - {step}", "dim"))
    45→    if len(completed) > 10:
    46→        print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(completed) - 10} more", "dim"))
    47→
    48→
    49→def _print_resolved_issues(resolved: dict[str, dict]) -> None:
    50→    """Print resolved issues delta since last triage."""
    51→    if not resolved:
    52→        return
    53→    print(colorize(f"\n  Resolved issues since last triage: {len(resolved)}", "cyan"))
    54→    for issue_id, issue in sorted(resolved.items())[:10]:
    55→        status = issue.get("status", "")
    56→        summary = issue.get("summary", "")
    57→        detail = issue.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(issue.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    58→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "")
    59→        print(f"    [{status}] [{dim}] {summary}")
    60→        print(colorize(f"      {issue_id}", "dim"))
    61→    if len(resolved) > 10:
    62→        print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(resolved) - 10} more", "dim"))
    63→
    64→
    65→def _print_recurring_patterns(open_issues: dict, resolved: dict[str, dict]) -> bool:
    66→    """Print recurring pattern diagnostics for reflect stage."""
    67→    recurring = detect_recurring_patterns(open_issues, resolved)
    68→    if not recurring:
    69→        return False
    70→    print(colorize("\n  Recurring patterns detected:", "yellow"))
    71→    for dim, info in sorted(recurring.items()):
    72→        resolved_count = len(info["resolved"])
    73→        open_count = len(info["open"])
    74→        label = "potential loop" if open_count >= resolved_count else "root cause unaddressed"
    75→        print(
    76→            colorize(
    77→                f"    {dim}: {resolved_count} resolved, {open_count} still open \u2014 {label}",
    78→                "yellow",
    79→            )
    80→        )
    81→    return True

   224→    if triage_sync.injected:
   225→        print(
   226→            colorize(
   227→                "  Plan: planning mode needed — review issues changed since last triage.",
   228→                "cyan",
   229→            )
   230→        )
   231→        append_log_entry(plan, "sync_triage", actor="system", detail={"injected": True})
   232→    return True
   233→
   234→
   235→def _sync_communicate_score_and_log(
   236→    plan: dict[str, object],
   237→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   238→    *,
   239→    policy,
   240→) -> bool:
   241→    communicate_sync = sync_communicate_score_needed(plan, state, policy=policy)
   242→    if not communicate_sync.changes:
   243→        return False
   244→    append_log_entry(
   245→        plan,
   246→        "sync_communicate_score",
   247→        actor="system",
   248→        detail={"injected": True},
   249→    )
   250→    return True
   251→
   252→
   253→def _sync_create_plan_and_log(
   254→    plan: dict[str, object],
   255→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   256→    *,
   257→    policy,
   258→) -> bool:
   259→    create_plan_sync = sync_create_plan_needed(plan, state, policy=policy)
   260→    if not create_plan_sync.changes:
   261→        return False
   262→    if create_plan_sync.injected:
   263→        print(
   264→            colorize(
   265→                "  Plan: reviews complete — `workflow::create-plan` queued.",
   266→                "cyan",
   267→            )
   268→        )
   269→        append_log_entry(plan, "sync_create_plan", actor="system", detail={"injected": True})
   270→    return True
   271→
   272→
   273→def _sync_plan_start_scores_and_log(
   274→    plan: dict[str, object],
   275→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   276→) -> bool:
   277→    seeded = _seed_plan_start_scores(plan, state)
   278→    if seeded:
   279→        append_log_entry(plan, "seed_start_scores", actor="system", detail={})
   280→        return True
   281→    # Only clear scores that existed before this reconcile pass —
   282→    # never clear scores we just seeded in the same scan.
   283→    cleared = _clear_plan_start_scores_if_queue_empty(state, plan)
   284→    if cleared:
   285→        append_log_entry(plan, "clear_start_scores", actor="system", detail={})
   286→    return cleared
   287→
   288→
   289→def reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime: Any) -> None:
   290→    """Reconcile plan queue metadata and stale subjective review dimensions."""
   291→    plan_path = runtime.state_path.parent / "plan.json" if runtime.state_path else None
   292→    try:
   293→        plan = load_plan(plan_path)
   294→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   295→        logger.warning("Plan reconciliation skipped (load failed): %s", exc)
   296→        return
   297→    dirty = False
   298→
   299→    if _apply_plan_reconciliation(plan, runtime.state, reconcile_plan_after_scan):
   300→        dirty = True
   301→
   302→    if _sync_unscored_and_log(plan, runtime.state):
   303→        dirty = True
   304→
   305→    target_strict, policy, cycle_just_completed = _subjective_policy_context(
   306→        runtime,
   307→        plan,
   308→    )
   309→    if _sync_stale_and_log(
   310→        plan,
   311→        runtime.state,
   312→        policy=policy,
   313→        cycle_just_completed=cycle_just_completed,
   314→    ):
   315→        dirty = True
   316→
   317→    if _sync_auto_clusters_and_log(
   318→        plan,
   319→        runtime.state,
   320→        target_strict=target_strict,
   321→        policy=policy,
   322→        cycle_just_completed=cycle_just_completed,
   323→    ):
   324→        dirty = True
   325→
   326→    if _sync_triage_and_log(plan, runtime.state):
   327→        dirty = True
   328→    if _sync_communicate_score_and_log(plan, runtime.state, policy=policy):
   329→        dirty = True
   330→    if _sync_create_plan_and_log(plan, runtime.state, policy=policy):
   331→        dirty = True
   332→    if _sync_plan_start_scores_and_log(plan, runtime.state):
   333→        dirty = True
   334→
   335→    if dirty:
   336→        try:
   337→            save_plan(plan, plan_path)
   338→        except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   339→            logger.warning("Plan reconciliation save failed: %s", exc)
   340→

1→"""Post-scan plan reconciliation — handle issue churn."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     6→from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
     7→
     8→from desloppify.engine._plan.annotations import get_issue_note
     9→from desloppify.engine._plan.operations_meta import append_log_entry
    10→from desloppify.engine._plan.operations_skip import resurface_stale_skips
    11→from desloppify.engine._plan.promoted_ids import prune_promoted_ids
    12→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import (
    13→    EPIC_PREFIX,
    14→    PlanModel,
    15→    SupersededEntry,
    16→    ensure_plan_defaults,
    17→)
    18→from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import (
    19→    SYNTHETIC_PREFIXES,
    20→    compute_new_issue_ids,
    21→    sync_triage_needed,
    22→)
    23→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, utc_now
    24→
    25→SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS = 90
    26→
    27→
    28→@dataclass
    29→class ReconcileResult:
    30→    """Summary of changes made during reconciliation."""
    31→
    32→    superseded: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    33→    pruned: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    34→    resurfaced: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    35→    changes: int = 0
    36→
    37→
    38→def _find_candidates(
    39→    state: StateModel, detector: str, file: str
    40→) -> list[str]:
    41→    """Find open issues that could be remaps for a disappeared issue."""
    42→    candidates: list[str] = []
    43→    for fid, issue in state.get("issues", {}).items():
    44→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
    45→            continue
    46→        if issue.get("detector") == detector and issue.get("file") == file:
    47→            candidates.append(fid)
    48→    return candidates
    49→
    50→
    51→def _is_issue_alive(state: StateModel, issue_id: str) -> bool:
    52→    """Return True if the issue exists and is open."""
    53→    issue = state.get("issues", {}).get(issue_id)
    54→    if issue is None:
    55→        return False
    56→    return issue.get("status") == "open"
    57→
    58→
    59→def _supersede_id(
    60→    plan: PlanModel,
    61→    state: StateModel,
    62→    issue_id: str,
    63→    now: str,
    64→) -> bool:
    65→    """Move a disappeared issue to superseded. Returns True if changed."""
    66→    issue = state.get("issues", {}).get(issue_id)
    67→    detector = ""
    68→    file = ""
    69→    summary = ""
    70→    if issue:
    71→        detector = issue.get("detector", "")
    72→        file = issue.get("file", "")
    73→        summary = issue.get("summary", "")
    74→
    75→    candidates = _find_candidates(state, detector, file) if detector else []
    76→    # Don't include the original in candidates
    77→    candidates = [c for c in candidates if c != issue_id]
    78→
    79→    entry: SupersededEntry = {
    80→        "original_id": issue_id,
    81→        "original_detector": detector,
    82→        "original_file": file,
    83→        "original_summary": summary,
    84→        "status": "superseded",
    85→        "superseded_at": now,
    86→        "remapped_to": None,
    87→        "candidates": candidates[:5],
    88→    }
    89→
    90→    # Preserve any existing override note
    91→    override_note = get_issue_note(plan, issue_id)
    92→    if override_note:
    93→        entry["note"] = override_note
    94→
    95→    plan["superseded"][issue_id] = entry
    96→
    97→    # Remove from queue_order, skipped, promoted_ids, cluster issue_ids
    98→    order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    99→    skipped: dict = plan.get("skipped", {})
   100→    if issue_id in order:
   101→        order.remove(issue_id)
   102→    skipped.pop(issue_id, None)
   103→    prune_promoted_ids(plan, {issue_id})
   104→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   105→        ids = cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   106→        if issue_id in ids:
   107→            ids.remove(issue_id)
   108→
   109→    # Clear stale cluster reference from override
   110→    override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(issue_id)
   111→    if override and override.get("cluster"):
   112→        override["cluster"] = None
   113→        override["updated_at"] = now
   114→
   115→    return True
   116→
   117→
   118→def _prune_old_superseded(plan: PlanModel, now_dt: datetime) -> list[str]:
   119→    """Remove superseded entries older than TTL. Returns pruned IDs."""
   120→    superseded = plan.get("superseded", {})
   121→    cutoff = now_dt - timedelta(days=SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS)
   122→    to_prune: list[str] = []
   123→
   124→    for fid, entry in superseded.items():
   125→        ts = entry.get("superseded_at", "")
   126→        try:
   127→            entry_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
   128→            if entry_dt.tzinfo is None:
   129→                entry_dt = entry_dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
   130→            if entry_dt < cutoff:
   131→                to_prune.append(fid)
   132→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   133→            to_prune.append(fid)
   134→
   135→    for fid in to_prune:
   136→        superseded.pop(fid, None)
   137→        # Also clean up stale overrides
   138→        plan.get("overrides", {}).pop(fid, None)
   139→
   140→    return to_prune
   141→
   142→
   143→def reconcile_plan_after_scan(
   144→    plan: PlanModel,
   145→    state: StateModel,
   146→) -> ReconcileResult:
   147→    """Reconcile plan against current state after a scan.
   148→
   149→    Finds IDs referenced in the plan that no longer exist or are no longer
   150→    open, moves them to superseded, and prunes old superseded entries.
   151→    """
   152→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   153→    result = ReconcileResult()
   154→    now = utc_now()
   155→    now_dt = datetime.now(UTC)
   156→
   157→    # Collect all issue IDs referenced by the plan
   158→    referenced_ids: set[str] = set()
   159→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   160→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   161→    for override_id in plan.get("overrides", {}):
   162→        referenced_ids.add(override_id)
   163→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   164→        referenced_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   165→
   166→    # Exclude already-superseded IDs and synthetic IDs (managed by stale_dimensions)
   167→    already_superseded = set(plan.get("superseded", {}).keys())
   168→    referenced_ids -= already_superseded
   169→    referenced_ids = {
   170→        fid for fid in referenced_ids
   171→        if not any(fid.startswith(prefix) for prefix in SYNTHETIC_PREFIXES)
   172→    }
   173→
   174→    # Check each referenced ID
   175→    for fid in sorted(referenced_ids):
   176→        if not _is_issue_alive(state, fid):
   177→            if _supersede_id(plan, state, fid, now):
   178→                result.superseded.append(fid)
   179→                result.changes += 1
   180→
   181→    # Reconcile epic clusters: remove dead issues, delete empty epics
   182→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   183→    epic_names_to_delete: list[str] = []
   184→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   185→        if not name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX):
   186→            continue
   187→        issue_ids = cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   188→        alive_ids = [fid for fid in issue_ids if _is_issue_alive(state, fid)]
   189→        if alive_ids != issue_ids:
   190→            cluster["issue_ids"] = alive_ids
   191→            result.changes += 1
   192→        if not alive_ids:
   193→            epic_names_to_delete.append(name)
   194→    for name in epic_names_to_delete:
   195→        clusters.pop(name, None)
   196→        result.changes += 1
   197→
   198→    # Resurface stale temporary skips
   199→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   200→
   201→    resurfaced = resurface_stale_skips(plan, scan_count)
   202→    if resurfaced:
   203→        result.resurfaced = resurfaced
   204→        result.changes += len(resurfaced)
   205→
   206→    # Prune old superseded entries
   207→    pruned = _prune_old_superseded(plan, now_dt)
   208→    result.pruned = pruned
   209→    result.changes += len(pruned)
   210→
   211→    # Log reconciliation if any changes were made
   212→    if result.changes > 0:
   213→        append_log_entry(
   214→            plan,
   215→            "reconcile",
   216→            issue_ids=result.superseded,
   217→            actor="system",
   218→            detail={
   219→                "superseded_count": len(result.superseded),
   220→                "pruned_count": len(result.pruned),
   221→                "resurfaced_count": len(result.resurfaced),
   222→            },
   223→        )
   224→
   225→    return result
   226→
   227→
   228→@dataclass
   229→class ReviewImportSyncResult:
   230→    """Summary of plan changes after a review import."""
   231→
   232→    new_ids: set[str]
   233→    added_to_queue: list[str]
   234→    triage_injected: bool
   235→
   236→
   237→def sync_plan_after_review_import(
   238→    plan: PlanModel,
   239→    state: StateModel,
   240→) -> ReviewImportSyncResult | None:
   241→    """Sync plan queue after review import. Pure engine function — no I/O.
   242→
   243→    Appends new issue IDs to queue_order and injects triage stages
   244→    if needed. Returns None when there are no new issues to sync.
   245→    """
   246→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   247→    new_ids = compute_new_issue_ids(plan, state)
   248→    if not new_ids:
   249→        return None
   250→
   251→    # Add new issue IDs to end of queue_order so they have position
   252→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   253→    existing = set(order)
   254→    added: list[str] = []
   255→    for fid in sorted(new_ids):
   256→        if fid not in existing:
   257→            order.append(fid)
   258→            added.append(fid)
   259→
   260→    # Inject triage stages if needed
   261→    triage_result = sync_triage_needed(plan, state)
   262→    triage_injected = bool(
   263→        triage_result and getattr(triage_result, "injected", False)
   264→    )
   265→
   266→    return ReviewImportSyncResult(
   267→        new_ids=new_ids,
   268→        added_to_queue=added,
   269→        triage_injected=triage_injected,
   270→    )
   271→
   272→
   273→__all__ = [
   274→    "ReconcileResult",
   275→    "ReviewImportSyncResult",
   276→    "reconcile_plan_after_scan",
   277→    "sync_plan_after_review_import",
   278→]
   279→

   190→def ensure_plan_defaults(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   191→    """Normalize a loaded plan to ensure all keys exist.
   192→
   193→    Runtime contract is v7-only. Legacy payloads are upgraded in-place once.
   194→    """
   195→    defaults = empty_plan()
   196→    for key, value in defaults.items():
   197→        plan.setdefault(key, value)

   201→def triage_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Cluster]:
   202→    """Return clusters whose name starts with ``EPIC_PREFIX``."""
   203→    return {
   204→        name: cluster
   205→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   206→        if name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   207→    }
   208→
   209→
   210→def validate_plan(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   211→    """Raise ValueError when plan invariants are violated."""
   212→    if not isinstance(plan.get("version"), int):
   213→        raise ValueError("plan.version must be an int")
   214→    if not isinstance(plan.get("queue_order"), list):
   215→        raise ValueError("plan.queue_order must be a list")
   216→
   217→    # No ID should appear in both queue_order and skipped
   218→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   219→    overlap = set(plan["queue_order"]) & skipped_ids
   220→    if overlap:
   221→        raise ValueError(
   222→            f"IDs cannot appear in both queue_order and skipped: {sorted(overlap)}"
   223→        )
   224→
   225→    # Validate skip entry kinds
   226→    for fid, entry in plan.get("skipped", {}).items():
   227→        kind = entry.get("kind")
   228→        if kind not in VALID_SKIP_KINDS:
   229→            raise ValueError(
   230→                f"Invalid skip kind {kind!r} for {fid}; must be one of {sorted(VALID_SKIP_KINDS)}"
   231→            )

   130→def triage_phase_banner(plan: PlanModel) -> str:
   131→    """Return a banner string when triage stage IDs are in the queue."""
   132→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   133→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   134→    has_triage = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   135→    if not has_triage:

   137→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   138→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   139→    completed = [s for s in ("observe", "reflect", "organize") if s in stages]
   140→    if completed:
   141→        return (
   142→            f"TRIAGE MODE ({len(completed)}/4 stages complete) — "
   143→            "complete all stages to exit. Run: desloppify plan triage"
   144→        )
   145→    return (
   146→        "TRIAGE MODE — review issues need analysis before fixing. "

   113→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   114→# Helpers for sync_stale_dimensions / sync_unscored_dimensions

   116→
   117→def _has_objective_backlog(
   118→    state: StateModel,
   119→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None,
   120→) -> bool:
   121→    """Return whether an objective backlog exists (open non-subjective issues)."""
   122→    if policy is not None:
   123→        return policy.has_objective_backlog
   124→    return any(
   125→        f.get("status") == "open"
   126→        and f.get("detector") not in _NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   127→        and not f.get("suppressed")
   128→        for f in state.get("issues", {}).values()
   129→    )

   131→
   132→def _prune_subjective_ids(
   133→    order: list[str],
   134→    *,
   135→    keep_ids: set[str],
   136→    pruned: list[str],
   137→) -> None:
   138→    """Remove subjective IDs from *order* that are not in *keep_ids*, appending removed to *pruned*."""
   139→    to_remove = [
   140→        fid for fid in order
   141→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   142→        and fid not in keep_ids
   143→    ]
   144→    for fid in to_remove:
   145→        order.remove(fid)
   146→        pruned.append(fid)
   147→
   148→
   149→def _inject_subjective_ids(
   150→    order: list[str],
   151→    plan: PlanModel,
   152→    *,
   153→    inject_ids: set[str],
   154→    to_front: bool,
   155→    injected: list[str],
   156→) -> None:
   157→    """Inject subjective IDs into *order* if not already present.
   158→
   159→    When *to_front* is True, inserts after promoted items (front of queue).
   160→    Otherwise appends to the back.
   161→    """
   162→    existing = set(order)
   163→    if to_front:
   164→        insert_at = promoted_insertion_index(order, plan)
   165→        for sid in reversed(sorted(inject_ids)):
   166→            if sid not in existing:
   167→                order.insert(insert_at, sid)
   168→                injected.append(sid)
   169→    else:
   170→        for sid in sorted(inject_ids):
   171→            if sid not in existing:
   172→                order.append(sid)
   173→                injected.append(sid)
   174→

   176→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   177→# Helpers for sync_triage_needed
   178→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   179→
   180→def _open_review_issue_ids(state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
   181→    """Return set of open issue IDs whose detector is 'review' or 'concerns'."""
   182→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   183→    return {
   184→        fid for fid, f in issues.items()
   185→        if f.get("status") == "open"
   186→        and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   187→    }
   188→
   189→
   190→def _new_review_ids_since_triage(
   191→    state: StateModel,
   192→    meta: dict,
   193→) -> set[str]:
   194→    """Return review issue IDs that are new since the last triage."""
   195→    current_review_ids = _open_review_issue_ids(state)
   196→    triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
   197→    return current_review_ids - triaged_ids
   198→
   199→
   200→def _prune_all_triage_stages(order: list[str]) -> None:
   201→    """Remove all ``triage::*`` stage IDs from *order*."""
   202→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
   203→        while sid in order:
   204→            order.remove(sid)
   205→
   206→
   207→def _inject_pending_triage_stages(
   208→    order: list[str],
   209→    plan: PlanModel,
   210→    confirmed: set[str],
   211→) -> bool:
   212→    """Inject triage stages for pending (unconfirmed) items.
   213→
   214→    Returns True if any stages were injected.
   215→    """
   216→    insert_at = promoted_insertion_index(order, plan)
   217→    stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit")
   218→    existing = set(order)
   219→    injected_count = 0
   220→    for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names, strict=False):
   221→        if name not in confirmed and sid not in existing:
   222→            order.insert(insert_at + injected_count, sid)
   223→            injected_count += 1
   224→    return injected_count > 0
   225→

   227→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   228→# Unscored dimension sync (front of queue, unconditional)
   229→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   230→
   231→def sync_unscored_dimensions(
   232→    plan: PlanModel,
   233→    state: StateModel,
   234→) -> UnscoredDimensionSyncResult:
   235→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions.
   236→
   237→    1. **Prune** — remove ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are
   238→       no longer unscored AND not stale (avoids pruning stale IDs — that is
   239→       ``sync_stale_dimensions``' responsibility).
   240→    2. **Inject** — unconditionally prepend currently-unscored IDs to the
   241→       *front* of ``queue_order`` so initial reviews are the first priority.
   242→    """
   243→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   244→    result = UnscoredDimensionSyncResult()
   245→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   246→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   247→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   248→
   249→    # --- Cleanup: prune subjective IDs that are no longer unscored --------
   250→    # Only prune IDs that are neither unscored nor stale (stale sync owns those).
   251→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=unscored_ids | stale_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   252→
   253→    # --- Inject: prepend unscored IDs after any promoted items -------------
   254→    _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=unscored_ids, to_front=True, injected=result.injected)
   255→
   256→    return result
   257→
   258→
   259→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   260→# Stale dimension sync (back of queue, conditional)
   261→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   262→
   263→def sync_stale_dimensions(
   264→    plan: PlanModel,
   265→    state: StateModel,
   266→    *,
   267→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   268→    cycle_just_completed: bool = False,
   269→) -> StaleDimensionSyncResult:
   270→    """Keep the plan queue in sync with stale and under-target subjective dimensions.
   271→
   272→    1. Remove any ``subjective::*`` IDs from ``queue_order`` that are no
   273→       longer stale/under-target and not unscored (avoids pruning IDs owned
   274→       by ``sync_unscored_dimensions``).
   275→    2. Inject stale and under-target dimension IDs when either:
   276→       a. No objective items remain (mid-cycle: append to back), OR
   277→       b. A cycle just completed (post-cycle: insert at front so subjective
   278→          review takes priority over new objective issues).
   279→    """
   280→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   281→    result = StaleDimensionSyncResult()
   282→    stale_ids = _current_stale_ids(state)
   283→    under_target_ids = current_under_target_ids(state)
   284→    injectable_ids = stale_ids | under_target_ids
   285→    unscored_ids = current_unscored_ids(state)
   286→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   287→
   288→    # --- Cleanup: prune resolved subjective IDs --------------------------
   289→    # Only prune IDs that are no longer injectable and not unscored.
   290→    _prune_subjective_ids(order, keep_ids=injectable_ids | unscored_ids, pruned=result.pruned)
   291→
   292→    # --- Inject or evict stale + under-target dimensions -----------------
   293→    has_real_items = _has_objective_backlog(state, policy)
   294→    should_inject = not has_real_items or cycle_just_completed
   295→
   296→    if not should_inject:
   297→        # Mid-cycle with objective backlog: evict any stale/under-target IDs
   298→        # that are present in the queue.  They may have been grandfathered from
   299→        # the unscored phase and should not be visible until the objective
   300→        # backlog clears or a cycle completes.
   301→        to_evict = [
   302→            fid for fid in order
   303→            if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   304→            and fid in injectable_ids
   305→        ]
   306→        for fid in to_evict:
   307→            order.remove(fid)
   308→            result.pruned.append(fid)
   309→
   310→    if should_inject and injectable_ids:
   311→        to_front = cycle_just_completed and has_real_items
   312→        _inject_subjective_ids(order, plan, inject_ids=injectable_ids, to_front=to_front, injected=result.injected)
   313→
   314→    return result
   315→

   317→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   318→# Triage snapshot hash + sync
   319→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   320→
   321→def review_issue_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:
   322→    """Hash open review issue IDs to detect changes.
   323→
   324→    Returns empty string when there are no open review issues.
   325→    """
   326→    return stale_policy_mod.review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)

   329→@dataclass
   330→class TriageSyncResult:
   331→    """What changed during a triage sync."""
   332→
   333→    injected: bool = False
   334→    pruned: bool = False
   335→
   336→    @property
   337→    def changes(self) -> int:
   338→        return int(self.injected) + int(self.pruned)

   340→
   341→def sync_triage_needed(
   342→    plan: PlanModel,
   343→    state: StateModel,
   344→) -> TriageSyncResult:
   345→    """Inject 4 triage stage IDs at front of queue when review issues change.
   346→
   347→    Only injects stages not already confirmed in ``epic_triage_meta``.
   348→
   349→    When stages are already present but all new issues have been resolved
   350→    since injection, auto-prunes the stale stages and updates the hash.
   351→
   352→    When issues are *resolved* (current IDs are a subset of previously
   353→    triaged IDs), the snapshot hash is updated silently — no re-triage
   354→    is needed since the user is working through the plan.
   355→    """
   356→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   357→    result = TriageSyncResult()
   358→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   359→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   360→    confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   361→
   362→    # Check if any triage stage is already in queue
   363→    already_present = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   364→
   365→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   366→    last_hash = meta.get("issue_snapshot_hash", "")
   367→
   368→    if already_present:
   369→        # Stages present — check if the reason for injection still applies.
   370→        # Only auto-prune when triage was completed before (hash exists),
   371→        # all new issues have been resolved, and no triage work is in
   372→        # progress.  This avoids pruning the initial triage or a
   373→        # user-started triage session.
   374→        if last_hash and not confirmed:
   375→            new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   376→
   377→            if not new_since_triage:
   378→                # No new issues remain — prune stale stages
   379→                _prune_all_triage_stages(order)
   380→                if current_hash:
   381→                    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   382→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   383→                result.pruned = True
   384→        return result
   385→
   386→    if current_hash and current_hash != last_hash:
   387→        # Distinguish "new issues appeared" from "issues were resolved".
   388→        # Only re-triage when genuinely new issues exist.
   389→        new_since_triage = _new_review_ids_since_triage(state, meta)
   390→
   391→        if new_since_triage:
   392→            # New review issues appeared — re-triage needed
   393→            result.injected = _inject_pending_triage_stages(order, plan, confirmed)
   394→        else:
   395→            # Only resolved issues changed the hash — update silently
   396→            meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   397→            plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   398→
   399→    return result

   412→
   413→def sync_score_checkpoint_needed(
   414→    plan: PlanModel,
   415→    state: StateModel,
   416→    *,
   417→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   418→) -> ScoreCheckpointSyncResult:
   419→    """Inject ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` when all initial reviews complete.
   420→
   421→    Injects when:
   422→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   423→    - ``workflow::score-checkpoint`` is not already in the queue
   424→
   425→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan
   426→    so the user sees their updated strict score right after reviews finish.
   427→    """
   428→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   429→    result = ScoreCheckpointSyncResult()
   430→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   431→
   432→    if WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   433→        return result
   434→
   435→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   436→    if policy is not None:
   437→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   438→            return result
   439→    else:
   440→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   441→        if unscored:
   442→            return result
   443→
   444→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   445→    insert_at = 0
   446→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   447→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   448→            insert_at = i + 1
   449→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID)
   450→    result.injected = True
   451→    return result
   452→
   453→
   454→@dataclass
   455→class CreatePlanSyncResult:
   456→    """What changed during a create-plan sync."""
   457→
   458→    injected: bool = False
   459→
   460→    @property
   461→    def changes(self) -> int:
   462→        return int(self.injected)
   463→
   464→
   465→def sync_create_plan_needed(
   466→    plan: PlanModel,
   467→    state: StateModel,
   468→    *,
   469→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   470→) -> CreatePlanSyncResult:
   471→    """Inject ``workflow::create-plan`` when reviews complete + objective backlog exists.
   472→
   473→    Only injects when:
   474→    - No unscored (placeholder) subjective dimensions remain
   475→    - At least one objective issue exists
   476→    - ``workflow::create-plan`` is not already in the queue
   477→    - No triage stages are pending
   478→    """
   479→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   480→    result = CreatePlanSyncResult()
   481→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   482→
   483→    if WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID in order:
   484→        return result
   485→
   486→    # Don't inject if triage stages are pending
   487→    if any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS):
   488→        return result
   489→
   490→    # Check that no unscored dimensions remain
   491→    if policy is not None:
   492→        if policy.unscored_ids:
   493→            return result
   494→        has_objective = policy.has_objective_backlog
   495→    else:
   496→        unscored = current_unscored_ids(state)
   497→        if unscored:
   498→            return result
   499→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   500→        has_objective = any(
   501→            f.get("status") == "open"
   502→            and f.get("detector") not in _NON_OBJECTIVE_DETECTORS
   503→            for f in issues.values()
   504→        )
   505→    if not has_objective:
   506→        return result
   507→
   508→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items, at the end of the
   509→    # synthetic block (so create-plan comes after score-checkpoint).
   510→    insert_at = 0
   511→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   512→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(TRIAGE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   513→            insert_at = i + 1
   514→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID)
   515→    result.injected = True
   516→    return result
   517→
   518→
   519→def compute_new_issue_ids(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
   520→    """Return the set of open review/concerns issue IDs added since last triage.
   521→
   522→    Returns an empty set when no prior triage has recorded ``triaged_ids``.
   523→    """
   524→    return stale_policy_mod.compute_new_issue_ids(plan, state)
   525→
   526→
   527→def is_triage_stale(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> bool:
   528→    """Side-effect-free check: is triage needed?
   529→
   530→    Returns True when genuinely *new* review issues appeared since the
   531→    last triage.  Triage stage IDs being in the queue alone is not
   532→    sufficient — the new issues that triggered injection may have been
   533→    resolved since then.
   534→
   535→    When issues are merely resolved (current IDs are a subset of
   536→    previously triaged IDs), triage is NOT stale — the user is working
   537→    through the plan.
   538→    """
   539→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   540→    return stale_policy_mod.is_triage_stale(plan, state, triage_ids=TRIAGE_IDS)
   541→
   542→
   543→@dataclass
   544→class ImportScoresSyncResult:
   545→    """What changed during an import-scores sync."""
   546→
   547→    injected: bool = False
   548→
   549→    @property
   550→    def changes(self) -> int:
   551→        return int(self.injected)
   552→
   553→
   554→def sync_import_scores_needed(
   555→    plan: PlanModel,
   556→    state: StateModel,
   557→    *,
   558→    assessment_mode: str | None = None,
   559→) -> ImportScoresSyncResult:
   560→    """Inject ``workflow::import-scores`` after issues-only import.
   561→
   562→    Only injects when:
   563→    - Assessment mode was ``issues_only`` (scores were skipped)
   564→    - ``workflow::import-scores`` is not already in the queue
   565→    - There are assessments in the payload that could be imported
   566→
   567→    Positioned after score-checkpoint, before create-plan.
   568→    """
   569→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   570→    result = ImportScoresSyncResult()
   571→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   572→
   573→    if WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID in order:
   574→        return result
   575→
   576→    # Only inject when scores were skipped (issues-only mode)
   577→    if assessment_mode != "issues_only":
   578→        return result
   579→
   580→    # Insert after any subjective/workflow items
   581→    insert_at = 0
   582→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   583→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) or fid.startswith(WORKFLOW_PREFIX):
   584→            insert_at = i + 1
   585→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_IMPORT_SCORES_ID)
   586→    result.injected = True
   587→    return result
   588→
   589→
   590→@dataclass
   591→class CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   592→    """What changed during a communicate-score sync."""
   593→
   594→    injected: bool = False
   595→
   596→    @property
   597→    def changes(self) -> int:
   598→        return int(self.injected)
   599→
   600→
   601→def sync_communicate_score_needed(
   602→    plan: PlanModel,
   603→    state: StateModel,
   604→    *,
   605→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None,
   606→    scores_just_imported: bool = False,
   607→) -> CommunicateScoreSyncResult:
   608→    """Inject ``workflow::communicate-score`` when scores should be shown.
   609→
   610→    Injects when either:
   611→    - All initial subjective reviews are complete (no unscored dimensions), OR
   612→    - Scores were just imported (trusted/attested/override)
   613→
   614→    And ``workflow::communicate-score`` is not already in the queue.
   615→    Positioned after subjective items but before triage/create-plan.
   616→    """
   617→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   618→    result = CommunicateScoreSyncResult()
   619→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   620→
   621→    # Also treat legacy score-checkpoint as already-present
   622→    if WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID in order or WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID in order:
   623→        return result
   624→
   625→    # Trigger 1: scores just imported
   626→    should_inject = scores_just_imported
   627→
   628→    # Trigger 2: all initial reviews complete (no unscored dimensions)
   629→    if not should_inject:
   630→        if policy is not None:
   631→            should_inject = not policy.unscored_ids
   632→        else:
   633→            should_inject = not current_unscored_ids(state)
   634→
   635→    if not should_inject:
   636→        return result
   637→
   638→    # Insert after any subjective items, before triage/workflow/issues
   639→    insert_at = 0
   640→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   641→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX):
   642→            insert_at = i + 1
   643→    order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_COMMUNICATE_SCORE_ID)
   644→    result.injected = True
   645→    return result
   646→

   329→def render_terminal_items(

   347→
   348→    if group != "item":
   349→        _render_grouped(items, group)
   350→        return
   351→
   352→    # Detect cluster drill-in: multiple items with cluster focus active
   353→    is_cluster_drill = len(items) > 1 and (
   354→        cluster_filter or (plan and plan.get("active_cluster"))
   355→    )
   356→

   363→            continue

    24→def _cmd_commit_log_status(plan: dict) -> None:

    56→    if not uncommitted and not commit_log:

    61→def _cmd_commit_log_record(args: argparse.Namespace, plan: dict) -> None:
    62→    """Record a commit: capture HEAD, move uncommitted → committed, update PR."""
    63→    sha = getattr(args, "sha", None)
    64→    branch = getattr(args, "branch", None)
    65→    note = getattr(args, "note", None)
    66→    only_patterns: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "only", None)
    67→
    68→    # Auto-detect from git if not overridden

    71→        if git.available:
    72→            sha = sha or git.head_sha
    73→            branch = branch or git.branch
    74→        elif not sha:

    76→            return

   159→        print(header)

   186→def cmd_commit_log_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

   188→    config = load_config()
   189→    if not config.get("commit_tracking_enabled", True):

   191→        return

   165→        print(colorize("\n  Queue cleared (1 workflow step)", "bold"))
   166→    else:
   167→        print(colorize(f"\n  Queue: {total} item{'s' if total != 1 else ''}", "bold"))
   168→
   169→
   170→def show_empty_queue(
   171→    queue: dict,
   172→    strict: float | None,
   173→    *,
   174→    plan_start_strict: float | None = None,
   175→    target_strict: float | None = None,
   176→) -> bool:
   177→    del target_strict
   178→    if queue.get("items"):
   179→        return False
   180→    if plan_start_strict is not None and strict is not None:
   181→        delta = format_plan_delta(strict, plan_start_strict)
   182→        delta_str = f" ({delta})" if delta else ""
   183→        print(colorize("\n  Queue cleared!", "green"))
   184→        print(colorize(
   185→            f"  Frozen plan-start: strict {plan_start_strict:.1f} → Live estimate: strict {strict:.1f}{delta_str}",
   186→            "cyan",
   187→        ))
   188→        print(colorize(
   189→            "  Run `desloppify scan` now to finalize and reveal your updated score.",
   190→            "dim",
   191→        ))
   192→        return True
   193→
   194→    suffix = f" Strict score: {strict:.1f}/100" if strict is not None else ""
   195→    print(colorize(f"\n  Nothing to do!{suffix}", "green"))
   196→    return True
   197→
   198→
   199→def render_compact_item(item: dict, idx: int, total: int) -> None:
   200→    """One-line summary for cluster drill-in items after the first."""
   201→    confidence = item.get("confidence", "medium")
   202→    tag = effort_tag(item)
   203→    tag_str = f" {tag}" if tag else ""
   204→    fid = item.get("id", "")
   205→    short = fid.rsplit("::", 1)[-1][:8] if "::" in fid else fid
   206→    print(f"  [{idx + 1}/{total}] [{confidence}]{tag_str} {item.get('summary', '')}")
   207→    print(colorize(f"         {item.get('file', '')}  [{short}]", "dim"))
   208→
   209→
   210→__all__ = [
   211→    "effort_tag",
   212→    "is_auto_fix_command",

   217→    "scorecard_subjective",

   130→def triage_phase_banner(plan: PlanModel) -> str:
   131→    """Return a banner string when triage stage IDs are in the queue."""
   132→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   133→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   134→    has_triage = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)
   135→    if not has_triage:
   136→        return ""
   137→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   138→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   139→    completed = [s for s in ("observe", "reflect", "organize") if s in stages]
   140→    if completed:
   141→        return (
   142→            f"TRIAGE MODE ({len(completed)}/4 stages complete) — "
   143→            "complete all stages to exit. Run: desloppify plan triage"
   144→        )
   145→    return (
   146→        "TRIAGE MODE — review issues need analysis before fixing. "
   147→        "Run: desloppify plan triage"
   148→    )
   149→

1→"""Pure operations for commit tracking within the living plan."""
