   391→def do_run_batches(
   392→    args,
   393→    state,
   394→    lang,
   395→    state_file,
   396→    *,
   397→    config: dict[str, Any] | None,
   398→    run_stamp_fn,
   399→    load_or_prepare_packet_fn,
   400→    selected_batch_indexes_fn,
   401→    prepare_run_artifacts_fn,
   402→    run_codex_batch_fn,
   403→    execute_batches_fn,
   404→    collect_batch_results_fn,
   405→    print_failures_fn,
   406→    print_failures_and_raise_fn,
   407→    merge_batch_results_fn,
   408→    build_import_provenance_fn,
   409→    do_import_fn,
   410→    run_followup_scan_fn,
   411→    safe_write_text_fn,
   412→    colorize_fn,
   413→    project_root: Path,
   414→    subagent_runs_dir: Path,
   415→) -> None:
   416→    """Run holistic investigation batches with a local subagent runner."""
   417→    config = config or {}
   418→    runner = getattr(args, "runner", "codex")
   419→    validate_runner(runner, colorize_fn=colorize_fn)
   420→    allow_partial = bool(getattr(args, "allow_partial", False))
   421→    policy = resolve_batch_run_policy(args)
   422→    run_parallel = policy.run_parallel
   423→    max_parallel_batches = policy.max_parallel_batches
   424→    heartbeat_seconds = policy.heartbeat_seconds
   425→    batch_timeout_seconds = policy.batch_timeout_seconds
   426→    batch_max_retries = policy.batch_max_retries
   427→    batch_retry_backoff_seconds = policy.batch_retry_backoff_seconds
   428→    stall_warning_seconds = policy.stall_warning_seconds
   429→    stall_kill_seconds = policy.stall_kill_seconds
   430→
   431→    stamp = run_stamp_fn()
   432→    packet, immutable_packet_path, prompt_packet_path = load_or_prepare_packet_fn(
   433→        args,
   434→        state=state,
   435→        lang=lang,
   436→        config=config,
   437→        stamp=stamp,
   438→    )
   439→
   440→    scan_path = str(getattr(args, "path", ".") or ".")
   441→    packet_dimensions = normalize_dimension_list(packet.get("dimensions", []))
   442→    scored_dimensions = scored_dimensions_for_lang(lang.name)
   443→    print_preflight_dimension_scope_notice(
   444→        selected_dims=packet_dimensions,
   445→        scored_dims=scored_dimensions,
   446→        explicit_selection=bool(getattr(args, "dimensions", None)),
   447→        scan_path=scan_path,
   448→        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
   449→    )
   450→    suggested_prepare_cmd = f"desloppify review --prepare --path {scan_path}"
   451→    batches = explode_to_single_dimension(
   452→        require_batches(
   453→            packet,
   454→            colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
   455→            suggested_prepare_cmd=suggested_prepare_cmd,
   456→        )
   457→    )
   458→    raw_dim_prompts = packet.get("dimension_prompts")
   459→    packet_dimension_prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]] | None = (
   460→        raw_dim_prompts if isinstance(raw_dim_prompts, dict) else None
   461→    )
   462→
   463→    selected_indexes = selected_batch_indexes_fn(args, batch_count=len(batches))
   464→    total_batches = len(selected_indexes)
   465→    effective_workers = min(total_batches, max_parallel_batches) if run_parallel else 1
   466→    waves = max(1, math.ceil(total_batches / max(1, effective_workers)))
   467→    worst_case_seconds = waves * batch_timeout_seconds
   468→    worst_case_minutes = max(1, math.ceil(worst_case_seconds / 60))
   469→    print(
   470→        colorize_fn(
   471→            "  Runtime expectation: "
   472→            f"{total_batches} batch(es), workers={effective_workers}, "
   473→            f"timeout-per-batch={int(batch_timeout_seconds / 60)}m, "
   474→            f"worst-case upper bound ~{worst_case_minutes}m.",
   475→            "dim",
   476→        )
   477→    )
   478→    run_dir, logs_dir, prompt_files, output_files, log_files = prepare_run_artifacts_fn(
   479→        stamp=stamp,
   480→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   481→        batches=batches,
   482→        packet_path=prompt_packet_path,
   483→        run_root=subagent_runs_dir,
   484→        repo_root=project_root,
   485→        dimension_prompts=packet_dimension_prompts,
   486→    )
   487→    run_log_path = resolve_run_log_path(
   488→        getattr(args, "run_log_file", None),
   489→        project_root=project_root,
   490→        run_dir=run_dir,
   491→    )
   492→    append_run_log = make_run_log_writer(run_log_path)
   493→
   494→    append_run_log(
   495→        "run-start "
   496→        f"runner={runner} parallel={run_parallel} max_parallel={max_parallel_batches} "
   497→        f"timeout={batch_timeout_seconds}s heartbeat={heartbeat_seconds:.1f}s "
   498→        f"stall_warning={stall_warning_seconds}s stall_kill={stall_kill_seconds}s "
   499→        f"retries={batch_max_retries} "
   500→        f"retry_backoff={batch_retry_backoff_seconds:.1f}s upper_bound={worst_case_minutes}m "
   501→        f"selected={[idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes]}"
   502→    )
   503→    append_run_log(f"run-path {run_dir}")
   504→    append_run_log(f"packet {immutable_packet_path}")
   505→    append_run_log(f"blind-packet {prompt_packet_path}")
   506→    print(colorize_fn(f"  Live run log: {run_log_path}", "dim"))
   507→
   508→    if getattr(args, "dry_run", False):
   509→        print(
   510→            colorize_fn(
   511→                "  Dry run only: prompts generated, runner execution skipped.", "yellow"
   512→            )
   513→        )
   514→        print(colorize_fn(f"  Immutable packet: {immutable_packet_path}", "dim"))
   515→        print(colorize_fn(f"  Blind packet: {prompt_packet_path}", "dim"))
   516→        print(colorize_fn(f"  Prompts: {run_dir / 'prompts'}", "dim"))
   517→        append_run_log("run-finished dry-run")
   518→        return
   519→    tasks = build_batch_tasks(
   520→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   521→        prompt_files=prompt_files,
   522→        output_files=output_files,
   523→        log_files=log_files,
   524→        project_root=project_root,
   525→        run_codex_batch_fn=run_codex_batch_fn,
   526→    )
   527→
   528→    batch_positions = {batch_idx: pos + 1 for pos, batch_idx in enumerate(selected_indexes)}
   529→    summary_created_at = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
   530→    stall_warned_batches: set[int] = set()
   531→    batch_status: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {
   532→        str(idx + 1): {
   533→            "position": batch_positions.get(idx, 0),
   534→            "status": "pending",
   535→            "prompt_path": str(prompt_files[idx]),
   536→            "result_path": str(output_files[idx]),
   537→            "log_path": str(log_files[idx]),
   538→        }
   539→        for idx in selected_indexes
   540→    }
   541→
   542→    if run_parallel:
   543→        print(
   544→            colorize_fn(
   545→                "  Parallel runner config: "
   546→                f"max-workers={min(total_batches, max_parallel_batches)}, "
   547→                f"heartbeat={heartbeat_seconds:.1f}s",
   548→                "dim",
   549→            )
   550→        )
   551→
   552→    _report_progress = _build_progress_reporter(
   553→        batch_positions=batch_positions,
   554→        batch_status=batch_status,
   555→        stall_warned_batches=stall_warned_batches,
   556→        total_batches=total_batches,
   557→        stall_warning_seconds=stall_warning_seconds,
   558→        prompt_files=prompt_files,
   559→        output_files=output_files,
   560→        log_files=log_files,
   561→        append_run_log=append_run_log,
   562→        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
   563→    )
   564→
   565→    record_execution_issue = partial(_record_execution_issue, append_run_log)
   566→    run_summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   567→    summary_config = BatchRunSummaryConfig(
   568→        created_at=summary_created_at,
   569→        run_stamp=stamp,
   570→        runner=runner,
   571→        run_parallel=run_parallel,
   572→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   573→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   574→        max_parallel_batches=max_parallel_batches,
   575→        batch_timeout_seconds=batch_timeout_seconds,
   576→        batch_max_retries=batch_max_retries,
   577→        batch_retry_backoff_seconds=batch_retry_backoff_seconds,
   578→        heartbeat_seconds=heartbeat_seconds,
   579→        stall_warning_seconds=stall_warning_seconds,
   580→        stall_kill_seconds=stall_kill_seconds,
   581→        immutable_packet_path=immutable_packet_path,
   582→        prompt_packet_path=prompt_packet_path,
   583→        run_dir=run_dir,
   584→        logs_dir=logs_dir,
   585→        run_log_path=run_log_path,
   586→    )
   587→
   588→    def write_run_summary(*, successful_batches, failed_batches, interrupted=False, interruption_reason=None):
   589→        _write_run_summary_impl(
   590→            summary_path=run_summary_path,
   591→            summary_config=summary_config,
   592→            batch_status=batch_status,
   593→            successful_batches=successful_batches,
   594→            failed_batches=failed_batches,
   595→            safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text_fn,
   596→            colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
   597→            append_run_log_fn=append_run_log,
   598→            interrupted=interrupted,
   599→            interruption_reason=interruption_reason,
   600→        )
   601→
   602→    try:
   603→        execution_failures = execute_batches_fn(
   604→            tasks=tasks,
   605→            options=BatchExecutionOptions(
   606→                run_parallel=run_parallel,
   607→                max_parallel_workers=max_parallel_batches,
   608→                heartbeat_seconds=heartbeat_seconds,
   609→            ),
   610→            progress_fn=_report_progress,
   611→            error_log_fn=record_execution_issue,
   612→        )
   613→    except KeyboardInterrupt:
   614→        for idx in selected_indexes:
   615→            key = str(idx + 1)
   616→            state = batch_status.setdefault(
   617→                key,
   618→                {"position": batch_positions.get(idx, 0), "status": "pending"},
   619→            )
   620→            if state.get("status") in {"pending", "queued", "running"}:
   621→                state["status"] = "interrupted"
   622→        write_run_summary(

   624→            failed_batches=[],

   627→        )

   646→    if failures and (not allow_partial or not batch_results):

    60→def _compute_ts_destructure_props(content, lines):
    61→    long_destructures = re.findall(r"\{\s*(\w+(?:\s*,\s*\w+){8,})\s*\}", content)
    62→    if not long_destructures:
    63→        return None
    64→    max_props = max(len(d.split(",")) for d in long_destructures)
    65→    return max_props, f"destructure w/{max_props} props"

    67→
    68→def _compute_ts_inline_types(content, lines):
    69→    inline_types = len(

    71→    )
    72→    if inline_types > 3:
    73→        return inline_types, f"{inline_types} inline types"

   137→def phase_logs(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   138→    log_result = logs_detector_mod.detect_logs_result(path)
   139→    log_entries = log_result.entries
   140→    total_files = log_result.population_size
   141→    log_groups: dict[tuple, list] = defaultdict(list)
   142→    for e in log_entries:
   143→        log_groups[(e["file"], e["tag"])].append(e)
   144→    results = []
   145→    for (file, tag), entries in log_groups.items():
   146→        results.append(
   147→            make_issue(
   148→                "logs",
   149→                file,
   150→                tag,
   151→                tier=1,
   152→                confidence="high",
   153→                summary=f"{len(entries)} tagged logs [{tag}]",
   154→                detail={
   155→                    "count": len(entries),
   156→                    "lines": [e["line"] for e in entries[:20]],
   157→                },
   158→            )
   159→        )
   160→    log(f"         {len(log_entries)} instances → {len(results)} issues")
   161→    return results, {"logs": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_files)}
   162→
   163→
   164→def phase_unused(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   165→    entries, total_files = unused_detector_mod.detect_unused(path)
   166→    return make_unused_issues(entries, log), {
   167→        "unused": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_files),
   168→    }

   170→
   171→def phase_exports(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   172→    export_entries, total_exports = exports_detector_mod.detect_dead_exports(path)
   173→    results = []
   174→    for e in export_entries:
   175→        results.append(
   176→            make_issue(
   177→                "exports",
   178→                e["file"],
   179→                e["name"],
   180→                tier=2,
   181→                confidence="high",
   182→                summary=f"Dead export: {e['name']}",
   183→                detail={"line": e.get("line"), "kind": e.get("kind")},
   184→            )
   185→        )
   186→    log(f"         {len(export_entries)} instances → {len(results)} issues")
   187→    return results, {"exports": total_exports}

   189→
   190→def phase_deprecated(
   191→    path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract
   192→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   193→    dep_result = deprecated_detector_mod.detect_deprecated_result(path)
   194→    dep_entries = dep_result.entries
   195→    total_deprecated = dep_result.population_size
   196→    results = []
   197→    for e in dep_entries:
   198→        if e["kind"] == "property":
   199→            continue
   200→        tier = 1 if e["importers"] == 0 else 3
   201→        results.append(
   202→            make_issue(
   203→                "deprecated",
   204→                e["file"],
   205→                e["symbol"],
   206→                tier=tier,
   207→                confidence="high",
   208→                summary=f"Deprecated: {e['symbol']} ({e['importers']} importers)"
   209→                + (" → safe to delete" if e["importers"] == 0 else ""),
   210→                detail={"importers": e["importers"], "line": e["line"]},
   211→            )
   212→        )
   213→    log(
   214→        f"         {len(dep_entries)} instances → {len(results)} issues (properties suppressed)"
   215→    )
   216→    return results, {"deprecated": total_deprecated}

   219→# ── phase_structural sub-functions ─────────────────────────
   220→
   221→
   222→def _detect_structural_signals(
   223→    path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract
   224→) -> tuple[list[Issue], int]:
   225→    """Detect large files, complexity, god components, and mixed concerns.
   226→
   227→    Returns (merged structural issues, file_count from large-file detection).
   228→    """
   229→    structural: dict[str, dict] = {}
   230→
   231→    large_entries, file_count = large_detector_mod.detect_large_files(
   232→        path,
   233→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   234→        threshold=lang.large_threshold,
   235→    )
   236→    for e in large_entries:
   237→        add_structural_signal(
   238→            structural, e["file"], f"large ({e['loc']} LOC)", {"loc": e["loc"]}
   239→        )
   240→
   241→    complexity_entries, _ = complexity_detector_mod.detect_complexity(
   242→        path,
   243→        signals=TS_COMPLEXITY_SIGNALS,
   244→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   245→        threshold=lang.complexity_threshold,
   246→    )
   247→    for e in complexity_entries:
   248→        add_structural_signal(
   249→            structural,
   250→            e["file"],
   251→            f"complexity score {e['score']}",
   252→            {"complexity_score": e["score"], "complexity_signals": e["signals"]},
   253→        )
   254→        lang.complexity_map[e["file"]] = e["score"]
   255→
   256→    god_entries, _ = gods_detector_mod.detect_gods(
   257→        extract_ts_components(path), TS_GOD_RULES, min_reasons=2
   258→    )
   259→    for e in god_entries:
   260→        add_structural_signal(
   261→            structural,
   262→            e["file"],
   263→            f"{e['detail'].get('hook_total', 0)} hooks ({', '.join(e['reasons'][:2])})",
   264→            {
   265→                "hook_total": e["detail"].get("hook_total", 0),
   266→                "hook_reasons": e["reasons"],
   267→            },
   268→        )
   269→
   270→    concern_entries, _ = concerns_detector_mod.detect_mixed_concerns(path)
   271→    for e in concern_entries:
   272→        add_structural_signal(
   273→            structural,
   274→            e["file"],
   275→            f"mixed: {', '.join(e['concerns'][:3])}",
   276→            {"concerns": e["concerns"]},
   277→        )
   278→
   279→    results = merge_structural_signals(structural, log)
   280→    return results, file_count
   281→
   282→
   283→def _detect_flat_dirs(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], int]:
   284→    """Detect flat directories with too many files or missing sub-organization."""
   285→    results: list[Issue] = []
   286→    flat_entries, dir_count = flat_dirs_detector_mod.detect_flat_dirs(
   287→        path,
   288→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   289→        config=flat_dirs_detector_mod.FlatDirDetectionConfig(),
   290→    )
   291→    for e in flat_entries:
   292→        child_dir_count = int(e.get("child_dir_count", 0))
   293→        combined_score = int(e.get("combined_score", e.get("file_count", 0)))
   294→        results.append(
   295→            make_issue(
   296→                "flat_dirs",
   297→                e["directory"],
   298→                "",
   299→                tier=3,
   300→                confidence="medium",
   301→                summary=flat_dirs_detector_mod.format_flat_dir_summary(e),
   302→                detail={
   303→                    "file_count": e["file_count"],
   304→                    "child_dir_count": child_dir_count,
   305→                    "combined_score": combined_score,
   306→                    "kind": e.get("kind", "overload"),
   307→                    "parent_sibling_count": int(e.get("parent_sibling_count", 0)),
   308→                    "wrapper_item_count": int(e.get("wrapper_item_count", 0)),
   309→                    "sparse_child_count": int(e.get("sparse_child_count", 0)),
   310→                    "sparse_child_ratio": float(e.get("sparse_child_ratio", 0.0)),
   311→                    "sparse_child_file_threshold": int(
   312→                        e.get("sparse_child_file_threshold", 0)
   313→                    ),
   314→                },
   315→            )
   316→        )
   317→    if flat_entries:
   318→        log(
   319→            f"         flat dirs: {len(flat_entries)} overloaded directories "
   320→            "(files/subdirs/combined)"
   321→        )
   322→    return results, dir_count
   323→
   324→
   325→def _detect_props_bloat(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], int]:
   326→    """Detect bloated prop interfaces in TypeScript files."""
   327→    results: list[Issue] = []
   328→    props_thresh = lang.props_threshold
   329→    prop_entries, prop_count = props_detector_mod.detect_prop_interface_bloat(
   330→        path, threshold=props_thresh
   331→    )
   332→    for e in prop_entries:
   333→        pc = e["prop_count"]
   334→        # Tiered severity: 15-29=low, 30-49=medium, 50+=high
   335→        if pc >= 50:
   336→            conf, tier = "high", 4
   337→        elif pc >= 30:
   338→            conf, tier = "medium", 3
   339→        else:
   340→            conf, tier = "low", 3
   341→        results.append(
   342→            make_issue(
   343→                "props",
   344→                e["file"],
   345→                e["interface"],
   346→                tier=tier,
   347→                confidence=conf,
   348→                summary=f"Bloated {e.get('kind', 'props')}: {e['interface']} ({pc} fields)",
   349→                detail={
   350→                    "prop_count": pc,
   351→                    "line": e["line"],
   352→                    "kind": e.get("kind", "props"),
   353→                },
   354→            )
   355→        )
   356→    return results, prop_count
   357→
   358→
   359→def _detect_passthrough(path: Path) -> list[Issue]:
   360→    """Detect passthrough components that forward most props unchanged."""
   361→    results: list[Issue] = []
   362→    pt_entries = detect_passthrough_components(path)
   363→    for e in pt_entries:
   364→        results.append(
   365→            make_issue(
   366→                "props",
   367→                e["file"],
   368→                f"passthrough::{e['component']}",
   369→                tier=e["tier"],
   370→                confidence=e["confidence"],
   371→                summary=f"Passthrough component: {e['component']} "
   372→                f"({e['passthrough']}/{e['total_props']} props forwarded, {e['ratio']:.0%})",
   373→                detail={
   374→                    "passthrough": e["passthrough"],
   375→                    "total_props": e["total_props"],
   376→                    "ratio": e["ratio"],
   377→                    "line": e["line"],
   378→                    "passthrough_props": e["passthrough_props"],
   379→                    "direct_props": e["direct_props"],
   380→                },
   381→            )
   382→        )
   383→    return results
   384→
   385→
   386→def phase_structural(
   387→    path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract
   388→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   389→    structural_results, file_count = _detect_structural_signals(path, lang)
   390→    flat_results, dir_count = _detect_flat_dirs(path, lang)
   391→    props_results, prop_count = _detect_props_bloat(path, lang)
   392→    passthrough_results = _detect_passthrough(path)
   393→
   394→    results = structural_results + flat_results + props_results + passthrough_results
   395→    potentials = {
   396→        "structural": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, file_count),
   397→        "flat_dirs": dir_count,
   398→        "props": max(prop_count, len(passthrough_results)) if prop_count else len(passthrough_results),
   399→    }
   400→    return results, potentials

   406→def _detect_single_use(

   413→        )
   414→    )
   415→    single_entries = filter_entries(lang.zone_map, single_entries, "single_use")
   416→    issues = make_single_use_issues(
   417→        single_entries, lang.get_area, skip_dir_names={"commands"}, stderr_fn=log

   419→    return issues, single_entries, single_candidates

   422→def _detect_coupling_violations(
   423→    path: Path, graph: dict, lang: LangRuntimeContract, shared_prefix: str, tools_prefix: str
   424→) -> tuple[list[Issue], int]:

   427→        path, graph, shared_prefix=shared_prefix, tools_prefix=tools_prefix
   428→    )

   430→    results: list[Issue] = []

   432→        results.append(
   433→            make_issue(
   434→                "coupling",
   435→                e["file"],
   436→                e["target"],
   437→                tier=2,
   438→                confidence="high",
   439→                summary=f"Backwards coupling: shared imports {e['target']} (tool: {e['tool']})",
   440→                detail={
   441→                    "target": e["target"],
   442→                    "tool": e["tool"],
   443→                    "direction": e["direction"],
   444→                },
   445→            )
   446→        )
   447→    return results, coupling_edge_counts.eligible_edges

   468→                detail={

   481→def _detect_cycles_and_orphans(
   482→    path: Path, graph: dict, lang: LangRuntimeContract
   483→) -> tuple[list[Issue], int]:
   484→    """Detect import cycles and orphaned files. Returns (issues, total_graph_files)."""

   489→    orphan_entries, total_graph_files = orphaned_detector_mod.detect_orphaned_files(
   490→        path,
   491→        graph,
   492→        extensions=lang.extensions,
   493→        options=orphaned_detector_mod.OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   494→            extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   495→            extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   496→            dynamic_import_finder=deps_detector_mod.build_dynamic_import_targets,
   497→            alias_resolver=deps_detector_mod.ts_alias_resolver,
   498→        ),
   499→    )
   500→    orphan_entries = filter_entries(lang.zone_map, orphan_entries, "orphaned")
   501→    results.extend(make_orphaned_issues(orphan_entries, log))
   502→    return results, total_graph_files

   572→
   573→def _make_boundary_issues(
   574→    single_entries: list[dict],
   575→    path: Path,
   576→    graph: dict,
   577→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   578→    shared_prefix: str,
   579→    tools_prefix: str,
   580→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   581→    """Create boundary-candidate issues, deduplicated against single-use."""
   582→    single_use_emitted = set()
   583→    for e in single_entries:
   584→        is_size_ok = 50 <= e["loc"] <= 200
   585→        is_colocated = lang.get_area and (
   586→            lang.get_area(rel(e["file"])) == lang.get_area(e["sole_importer"])
   587→        )
   588→        if not is_size_ok and not is_colocated:
   589→            single_use_emitted.add(rel(e["file"]))
   590→
   591→    results = []
   592→    deduped = 0
   593→    boundary_entries, total_shared = coupling_detector_mod.detect_boundary_candidates(
   594→        path,
   595→        graph,
   596→        shared_prefix=shared_prefix,
   597→        tools_prefix=tools_prefix,
   598→        skip_basenames={"index.ts", "index.tsx"},
   599→    )
   600→    for e in boundary_entries:
   601→        if rel(e["file"]) in single_use_emitted:
   602→            deduped += 1
   603→            continue
   604→        results.append(
   605→            make_issue(
   606→                "coupling",
   607→                e["file"],
   608→                f"boundary::{e['sole_tool']}",
   609→                tier=3,
   610→                confidence="medium",
   611→                summary=f"Boundary candidate ({e['loc']} LOC): only used by {e['sole_tool']} "
   612→                f"({e['importer_count']} importers)",
   613→                detail={
   614→                    "sole_tool": e["sole_tool"],
   615→                    "importer_count": e["importer_count"],
   616→                    "loc": e["loc"],
   617→                },
   618→            )
   619→        )
   620→    if deduped:
   621→        log(f"         ({deduped} boundary candidates skipped — covered by single_use)")
   622→    return results, total_shared
   623→
   624→
   625→def phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   626→    results = []
   627→    graph = deps_detector_mod.build_dep_graph(path)
   628→    lang.dep_graph = graph
   629→    zm = lang.zone_map
   630→
   631→    # Single-use (shared helper)
   632→    single_use_issues, single_entries, single_candidates = _detect_single_use(path, graph, lang)
   633→    results.extend(single_use_issues)
   634→
   635→    src_path = get_src_path()
   636→    shared_prefix = f"{src_path}/shared/"
   637→    tools_prefix = f"{src_path}/tools/"
   638→
   639→    # Coupling violations
   640→    coupling_issues, coupling_edges = _detect_coupling_violations(
   641→        path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
   642→    )
   643→    results.extend(coupling_issues)
   644→
   645→    # TS-specific: boundary candidates (deduplicated against single-use)
   646→    boundary_issues, _ = _make_boundary_issues(
   647→        single_entries, path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
   648→    )
   649→    results.extend(boundary_issues)
   650→
   651→    # TS-specific: cross-tool imports
   652→    cross_tool_issues, cross_edges = _detect_cross_tool_imports(
   653→        path, graph, lang, tools_prefix
   654→    )
   655→    results.extend(cross_tool_issues)
   656→
   657→    # Cycles + orphaned (shared helpers)
   658→    cycle_orphan_issues, total_graph_files = _detect_cycles_and_orphans(path, graph, lang)
   659→    results.extend(cycle_orphan_issues)
   660→
   661→    # Re-export facades (shared detector)
   662→    results.extend(_detect_facades(graph, lang))
   663→
   664→    # TS-specific: pattern consistency
   665→    pattern_issues, total_areas = _detect_pattern_anomalies(path)
   666→    results.extend(pattern_issues)
   667→
   668→    # TS-specific: naming consistency
   669→    naming_issues, total_dirs = _detect_naming_inconsistencies(path, lang)
   670→    results.extend(naming_issues)
   671→
   672→    log(f"         → {len(results)} coupling/structural issues total")
   673→    potentials = {
   674→        "single_use": adjust_potential(zm, single_candidates),
   675→        "coupling": coupling_edges + cross_edges,
   676→        "cycles": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   677→        "orphaned": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   678→        "patterns": total_areas,
   679→        "naming": total_dirs,
   680→        "facade": adjust_potential(zm, total_graph_files),
   681→    }
   682→    return results, potentials
   683→
   684→
   685→def phase_smells(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   686→    smell_entries, total_smell_files = smells_detector_mod.detect_smells(path)
   687→    results = make_smell_issues(smell_entries, log)
   688→
   689→    # TS-specific: React state sync anti-patterns
   690→    react_entries, total_effects = react_detector_mod.detect_state_sync(path)
   691→    for e in react_entries:
   692→        setter_str = ", ".join(e["setters"])
   693→        results.append(
   694→            make_issue(
   695→                "react",
   696→                e["file"],
   697→                setter_str,
   698→                tier=3,
   699→                confidence="medium",
   700→                summary=f"State sync anti-pattern: useEffect only calls {setter_str}",
   701→                detail={"line": e["line"], "setters": e["setters"]},
   702→            )
   703→        )
   704→    if react_entries:
   705→        log(f"         react: {len(react_entries)} state sync anti-patterns")
   706→
   707→    # TS-specific: Context provider nesting depth
   708→    nesting_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_context_nesting(path)
   709→    for e in nesting_entries:
   710→        providers_str = " → ".join(e["providers"][:5])
   711→        results.append(
   712→            make_issue(
   713→                "react",
   714→                e["file"],
   715→                f"nesting::{e['depth']}",
   716→                tier=3,
   717→                confidence="medium",
   718→                summary=f"Deep provider nesting ({e['depth']} levels): {providers_str}",
   719→                detail={"depth": e["depth"], "providers": e["providers"]},
   720→            )
   721→        )
   722→    if nesting_entries:
   723→        log(f"         react: {len(nesting_entries)} deep provider nesting")
   724→
   725→    # TS-specific: Hook return bloat
   726→    hook_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_hook_return_bloat(path)
   727→    for e in hook_entries:
   728→        results.append(
   729→            make_issue(
   730→                "react",
   731→                e["file"],
   732→                f"hook_bloat::{e['hook']}",
   733→                tier=3,
   734→                confidence="medium",
   735→                summary=f"Hook return bloat: {e['hook']} returns {e['field_count']} fields",
   736→                detail={
   737→                    "hook": e["hook"],
   738→                    "field_count": e["field_count"],
   739→                    "line": e["line"],
   740→                },
   741→            )
   742→        )
   743→    if hook_entries:
   744→        log(f"         react: {len(hook_entries)} bloated hook returns")
   745→
   746→    # TS-specific: Boolean state explosion
   747→    bool_entries, _ = react_detector_mod.detect_boolean_state_explosion(path)
   748→    for e in bool_entries:
   749→        states_str = ", ".join(e["states"][:5])
   750→        results.append(
   751→            make_issue(
   752→                "react",
   753→                e["file"],
   754→                f"bool_state::{e['prefix']}",
   755→                tier=3,
   756→                confidence="low",
   757→                summary=f"Boolean state explosion: {e['count']} boolean useState hooks ({states_str})",
   758→                detail={

   760→                    "setters": e["setters"],
   761→                    "states": e["states"],
   762→                    "line": e["line"],
   763→                },
   764→            )
   765→        )
   766→    if bool_entries:
   767→        log(f"         react: {len(bool_entries)} boolean state explosions")
   768→
   769→    return results, {
   770→        "smells": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, total_smell_files),
   771→        "react": total_effects,
   772→    }

+"""CLI parser group builder for plan command family."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+
+
+def add_plan_parser(sub) -> None:
+    p_plan = sub.add_parser(
+        "plan",
+        help="Living plan: generate, show, resolve, skip, cluster, triage",
+        description="""\
+Manage the living plan — a persistent layer on top of the work queue.
+Track custom ordering, clusters, skips, and per-issue annotations.
+Run with no subcommand to generate a full prioritized markdown plan.""",
+        epilog="""\
+typical workflow:
+  desloppify scan                       # detect issues
+  desloppify plan                       # full prioritized markdown
+  desloppify plan queue                 # compact table of all items
+  desloppify plan cluster create ...    # group related issues
+  desloppify plan focus <cluster>       # narrow scope
+  desloppify next                       # work on the next item
+  desloppify plan resolve <id> --attest .. # mark as fixed
+
+patterns (used by reorder, skip, resolve, describe, note, etc.):
+  Patterns match issues by detector, file, ID prefix, glob, or name.
+  Cluster names also work as patterns — they expand to all member IDs.
+  Examples: "security", "src/foo.py", "unused::*React*", "my-cluster"
+
+subcommands:
+  show       Show plan metadata summary
+  queue      Compact table of upcoming queue items
+  reset      Reset plan to empty
+  reorder    Reposition issues or clusters in the queue
+  resolve    Mark issues as fixed (score movement + next-step)
+  describe   Set augmented description
+  note       Set note on issues
+  skip       Skip issues (temporary/permanent/false_positive)
+  unskip     Bring skipped issues back to queue
+  reopen     Reopen resolved issues
+  focus      Set or clear active cluster focus
+  cluster    Manage issue clusters
+  triage     Staged triage workflow (after review)""",
+        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
+    )
+    p_plan.add_argument("--state", type=str, default=None, help="Path to state file")
+    p_plan.add_argument(
+        "--output", type=str, metavar="FILE", help="Write to file instead of stdout"
+    )
+
+    plan_sub = p_plan.add_subparsers(dest="plan_action")
+
+    # plan show
+    plan_sub.add_parser("show", help="Show plan metadata summary")
+
+    # plan queue
+    p_queue = plan_sub.add_parser("queue", help="Compact table of upcoming queue items")
+    p_queue.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=30, help="Max items (default: 30, 0=all)")
+    p_queue.add_argument("--cluster", type=str, default=None, metavar="NAME",
+                         help="Filter to a specific cluster")
+    p_queue.add_argument("--include-skipped", action="store_true",
+                         help="Include skipped items at end")
+    p_queue.add_argument("--sort", choices=["priority", "recent"], default="priority",
+                         help="Sort order (default: priority)")
+
+    # plan reset
+    plan_sub.add_parser("reset", help="Reset plan to empty")
+
+    # plan reorder <patterns> <position> [--target TARGET]
+    p_move = plan_sub.add_parser(
+        "reorder",
+        help="Reposition issues in the queue",
+        epilog="""\
+patterns accept issue IDs, detector names, file paths, globs, or cluster names.
+cluster names expand to all member IDs automatically.
+
+examples:
+  desloppify plan reorder security top                         # all issues from detector
+  desloppify plan reorder "unused::src/foo.ts::*" top          # glob pattern

1→"""Structural signal helpers shared across language phase implementations."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import resolve_path
     8→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import count_lines
     9→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
    10→from desloppify.state import Issue, make_issue
    11→
    12→
    13→def add_structural_signal(structural: dict, file: str, signal: str, detail: dict):
    14→    """Add a complexity signal to the per-file structural dict.
    15→
    16→    Accumulates signals per file so they can be merged into tiered issues.
    17→    """
    18→    f = resolve_path(file)
    19→    structural.setdefault(f, {"signals": [], "detail": {}})
    20→    structural[f]["signals"].append(signal)
    21→    structural[f]["detail"].update(detail)
    22→
    23→
    24→def merge_structural_signals(
    25→    structural: dict,
    26→    stderr_fn,
    27→    *,
    28→    complexity_only_min: int = 35,
    29→) -> list[Issue]:
    30→    """Convert per-file structural signals into tiered issues.
    31→
    32→    3+ signals -> T4/high (needs decomposition).
    33→    1-2 signals -> T3/medium.
    34→    Complexity-only files (no large/god signals) need score >= complexity_only_min
    35→    to be flagged — lower complexity in small files is normal, not decomposition-worthy.
    36→    """
    37→    results = []
    38→    suppressed = 0
    39→    for filepath, data in structural.items():
    40→        if "loc" not in data["detail"]:
    41→            try:
    42→                p = (
    43→                    Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else get_project_root() / filepath
    44→                )
    45→                data["detail"]["loc"] = count_lines(p)
    46→            except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    47→                data["detail"]["loc"] = 0
    48→
    49→        # Suppress complexity-only issues below the elevated threshold.
    50→        signals = data["signals"]
    51→        is_complexity_only = all(s.startswith("complexity") for s in signals)
    52→        if is_complexity_only:
    53→            score = data["detail"].get("complexity_score", 0)
    54→            if score < complexity_only_min:
    55→                suppressed += 1
    56→                continue
    57→
    58→        signal_count = len(signals)
    59→        tier = 4 if signal_count >= 3 else 3
    60→        confidence = "high" if signal_count >= 3 else "medium"
    61→        summary = "Large file: " + " / ".join(signals)
    62→        results.append(
    63→            make_issue(
    64→                "structural",
    65→                filepath,
    66→                "",
    67→                tier=tier,
    68→                confidence=confidence,
    69→                summary=summary,
    70→                detail=data["detail"],
    71→            )
    72→        )
    73→    if suppressed:
    74→        stderr_fn(
    75→            "         "
    76→            f"{suppressed} complexity-only files below threshold (< {complexity_only_min})"
    77→        )
    78→    stderr_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} structural issues")
    79→    return results
    80→
    81→
    82→__all__ = ["add_structural_signal", "merge_structural_signals"]
    83→

   287→def _validate_run_dir(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, Path, str]:
   288→    """Validate run directory, load summary, and return (summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path).
   289→
   290→    Raises CommandError on any validation failure.
   291→    """
   292→    if not run_dir.is_dir():
   293→        raise CommandError(f"run directory not found: {run_dir}", exit_code=1)
   294→
   295→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   296→    if not summary_path.exists():
   297→        raise CommandError(f"no run_summary.json in {run_dir}", exit_code=1)
   298→    try:
   299→        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())
   300→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   301→        raise CommandError(f"Error reading run summary: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   302→
   303→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   304→    blind_packet_path = Path(str(summary.get("blind_packet", "")))
   305→    immutable_packet_path = str(summary.get("immutable_packet", ""))
   306→
   307→    if not successful:
   308→        raise CommandError("no successful batches in run summary.", exit_code=1)
   309→    if not blind_packet_path.exists():
   310→        raise PacketValidationError(f"blind packet not found: {blind_packet_path}", exit_code=1)
   311→
   312→    try:
   313→        packet = json.loads(Path(immutable_packet_path).read_text())
   314→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   315→        raise PacketValidationError(f"Error reading immutable packet: {exc}", exit_code=1) from exc
   316→
   317→    summary["_packet"] = packet
   318→    return summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path
   319→
   320→
   321→def do_import_run(
   322→    run_dir_path: str,
   323→    state: dict,
   324→    lang,
   325→    state_file: str,
   326→    *,
   327→    config: dict | None = None,
   328→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   329→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   330→    scan_path: str = ".",
   331→) -> None:
   332→    """Re-import results from a completed run directory.
   333→
   334→    Replays the merge+provenance+import step that normally runs at the end of
   335→    ``--run-batches``.  Useful when the original pipeline was interrupted (e.g.
   336→    broken pipe from background execution) but all batch results completed.
   337→    """
   338→    run_dir = Path(run_dir_path)
   339→    summary, blind_packet_path, _immutable_path = _validate_run_dir(run_dir)
   340→
   341→    runner = str(summary.get("runner", "codex"))
   342→    stamp = str(summary.get("run_stamp", ""))
   343→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   344→    packet = summary.pop("_packet", {})
   345→    allowed_dims = {str(d) for d in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(d, str)}
   346→
   347→    # -- locate and parse raw batch results --
   348→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   349→    selected_indexes = [idx - 1 for idx in successful]  # convert 1-based to 0-based
   350→    output_files = {
   351→        idx: results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   352→        for idx in selected_indexes
   353→    }
   354→
   355→    missing = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes if not output_files[idx].exists()]
   356→    if missing:
   357→        raise CommandError(f"missing result files for batches: {missing}", exit_code=1)
   358→
   359→    batch_results, failures = collect_batch_results(
   360→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   361→        failures=[],
   362→        output_files=output_files,
   363→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   364→        extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: batch_core_mod.extract_json_payload(raw, log_fn=log),
   365→        normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: batch_core_mod.normalize_batch_result(
   366→            payload,
   367→            dims,
   368→            max_batch_issues=max_batch_issues_for_dimension_count(len(dims)),
   369→            abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   370→        ),
   371→    )
   372→
   373→    if not batch_results:
   374→        raise CommandError("no valid batch results could be parsed.", exit_code=1)
   375→
   376→    print(colorize(f"  Parsed {len(batch_results)} batch results from {run_dir}", "bold"))
   377→    if failures:
   378→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {len(failures)} batches failed to parse: {[f + 1 for f in failures]}", "yellow"))
   379→
   380→    # -- merge --
   381→    merged = _merge_batch_results(batch_results)
   382→
   383→    # -- build provenance --
   384→    successful_indexes = [idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in set(failures)]
   385→    merged["provenance"] = build_batch_import_provenance(
   386→        runner=runner,
   387→        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   388→        run_stamp=stamp,
   389→        batch_indexes=successful_indexes,
   390→    )
   391→
   392→    # -- write merged output --
   393→    merged_path = run_dir / "holistic_issues_merged.json"
   394→    safe_write_text(merged_path, json.dumps(merged, indent=2) + "\n")
   395→    print(colorize(f"  Merged output: {merged_path}", "bold"))
   396→
   397→    # -- import with trusted source --
   398→    _do_import(
   399→        str(merged_path),
   400→        state,
   401→        lang,
   402→        state_file,
   403→        config=config,
   404→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   405→        trusted_assessment_source=True,
   406→        trusted_assessment_label=f"trusted import-run replay from {run_dir.name}",
   407→    )
   408→
   409→    # -- optional follow-up scan --
   410→    if scan_after_import:
   411→        lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))

patterns (used by reorder, skip, resolve, describe, note, etc.):

   211→    output_files: dict,

   215→) -> tuple[list[dict], list[int], list[int], set[int]]:
   216→    """Collect batch results and reconcile per-batch status entries.
   217→
   218→    Returns (batch_results, successful_indexes, failures, failure_set).
   219→    """

   244→            continue
   245→        if not output_files[idx].exists():

Now I have the complete picture. Let me create a comprehensive analysis document:

## Analysis Results: TypeScript phases.py Decomposition

I found **3 significant problems** in the decomposition of `phase_structural()` and `phase_coupling()`:

### **Problem 1: Type Mismatch in `_make_boundary_issues()` Return Type**

**Location:** Line 580  
**Issue:** Return type annotation is wrong

```python
def _make_boundary_issues(
    single_entries: list[dict],
    path: Path,
    graph: dict,
    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
    shared_prefix: str,
    tools_prefix: str,
) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:  # ❌ WRONG: says list[dict]
    """Create boundary-candidate issues, deduplicated against single-use."""
    ...
    return results, total_shared  # ✅ Actually returns tuple[list[Issue], int]
```

**Details:**
- Line 580 declares return type as `tuple[list[dict], int]`
- But line 622 actually returns `results` which contains `Issue` objects (created via `make_issue()` on line 605)
- The type should be `tuple[list[Issue], int]`
- This inconsistency is caught at the call site, line 646:

```python
boundary_issues, _ = _make_boundary_issues(
    single_entries, path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
)
results.extend(boundary_issues)  # ✅ Works correctly (Issue objects are expected)
```

The code actually works correctly because `phase_coupling()` treats the return as `list[Issue]`, but the annotation is false.

---

### **Problem 2: Unused Return Value from `_make_boundary_issues()`**

**Location:** Line 646  
**Issue:** Second return value (total_shared) is discarded with `_` but not recorded in potentials

```python
boundary_issues, _ = _make_boundary_issues(
    single_entries, path, graph, lang, shared_prefix, tools_prefix
)
results.extend(boundary_issues)
```

**Details:**
- `_make_boundary_issues()` returns `total_shared` (from line 593 `detect_boundary_candidates()`)
- This is the potential count for boundary candidates
- But it's thrown away with `_` on line 646
- The potentials dict (lines 673-681) has no entry for boundaries
- **Result**: No potential tracking for "boundary" detector, making this dimension invisible to scoring

Expected:
```python
boundary_issues, boundary_potential = _make_boundary_issues(...)
results.extend(boundary_issues)
# Later in potentials dict:
"boundary": adjust_potential(zm, boundary_potential),
```

---

### **Problem 3: Inconsistent Potentials Dict Value Types in `phase_structural()`**

**Location:** Lines 395-399  
**Issue:** Mixed types in potentials dict - some `int`, some return values from `adjust_potential()`

```python
potentials = {
    "structural": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, file_count),  # → int (adjusted)
    "flat_dirs": dir_count,                                     # → int (raw)
    "props": max(prop_count, len(passthrough_results)) if prop_count else len(passthrough_results),  # → int (raw)
}
```

**Details:**
- `"structural"` uses `adjust_potential()` which applies zone-map filtering
- `"flat_dirs"` and `"props"` are raw counts with no adjustment
- Other phases (e.g., `phase_coupling`, lines 673-681) apply `adjust_potential()` consistently to file/dir counts
- This creates inconsistency across phases
- Some dimensions are zone-adjusted, others are not
- **Result**: Scoring calculations may be biased for flat_dirs and props relative to other detectors

Expected consistent pattern:
```python
potentials = {
    "structural": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, file_count),
    "flat_dirs": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, dir_count),
    "props": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, prop_count),  # or similar
}
```

---

### **Problem 4: Type Mismatch in `_make_boundary_issues()` Parameter**

**Location:** Line 580  
**Secondary Issue:** Return type says `list[dict]` but constructor creates `Issue` objects

While not technically breaking (since Python doesn't enforce type hints at runtime), the annotation on line 580 is actively misleading:

```python
-> tuple[list[dict], int]:  # Declares dict
# but actually:
results.append(make_issue(...))  # Creates Issue
```

This violates Python typing contract and will fail mypy/pyright checks.

---

## Summary of Findings

| Problem | Severity | Line(s) | Fix |
|---------|----------|---------|-----|
| `_make_boundary_issues()` return type annotation wrong | High | 580 | Change `list[dict]` to `list[Issue]` |
| Boundary potential discarded, not recorded in dict | High | 646, 673-681 | Capture return value and add to potentials |
| Inconsistent zone adjustment in `phase_structural()` potentials | Medium | 395-399 | Apply `adjust_potential()` to `flat_dirs` and `props` |

All issues affect correctness of dimension scoring or type safety.

+def _build_progress_reporter(
+    *,
+    batch_positions: dict[int, int],
+    batch_status: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
+    stall_warned_batches: set[int],
+    total_batches: int,
+    stall_warning_seconds: float,
+    prompt_files: dict,
+    output_files: dict,
+    log_files: dict,
+    append_run_log,
+    colorize_fn,
+):
+    """Build the _report_progress closure used during batch execution."""
+
+    def _report_progress(
+        progress_event: BatchProgressEvent,
+    ) -> None:
+        batch_index = progress_event.batch_index
+        event = progress_event.event
+        code = progress_event.code
+        details = progress_event.details
+        if event == "heartbeat":
+            _handle_heartbeat(
+                details=details,
+                total_batches=total_batches,
+                stall_warning_seconds=stall_warning_seconds,
+                stall_warned_batches=stall_warned_batches,
+                append_run_log=append_run_log,
+                colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
+            )
+            return
+
+        position = batch_positions.get(batch_index, 0)
+        key = str(batch_index + 1)
+        state = batch_status.setdefault(
+            key,
+            {
+                "position": position,
+                "status": "pending",
+                "prompt_path": str(prompt_files.get(batch_index, "")),
+                "result_path": str(output_files.get(batch_index, "")),
+                "log_path": str(log_files.get(batch_index, "")),
+            },
+        )
+        if event == "queued":
+            state["status"] = "queued"
+            print(
+                colorize_fn(
+                    f"  Batch {position}/{total_batches} queued (#{batch_index + 1})",
+                    "dim",
+                )
+            )
+            append_run_log(f"batch-queued batch={batch_index + 1} position={position}/{total_batches}")
+            return
+        if event == "start":
+            state["status"] = "running"
+            state["started_at"] = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
+            print(
+                colorize_fn(
+                    f"  Batch {position}/{total_batches} started (#{batch_index + 1})",
+                    "dim",
+                )
+            )
+            append_run_log(f"batch-start batch={batch_index + 1} position={position}/{total_batches}")
+            return
+        if event == "done":
+            status = "done" if code == 0 else f"failed ({code})"
+            tone = "dim" if code == 0 else "yellow"
+            elapsed_seconds = details.get("elapsed_seconds")
